- **[host] ProcessRunner SIGPIPE-resilience fix (production crash + recurring gate-flake).** Diagnosed the recurring `JQRunnerTests.test_invalid_filter_throws` SIGPIPE (signal 13) flake (≥3× this session): `ProcessRunner` writes a child's stdin off-thread WITHOUT `F_SETNOSIGPIPE`, so a child that exits before reading all of stdin (jq rejecting an invalid filter — under load it wins the race) closes the read end → our `write(2)` raises SIGPIPE, which is fatal-by-default + UNCATCHABLE by the `try?` (a signal isn't a Swift throw) → kills the PARENT (the app / the test runner). This is a REAL production crash on an invalid jq filter, not just a test flake. Fix: `fcntl(writeFD, F_SETNOSIGPIPE, 1)` on the stdin write fd (mirrors LSPClient's existing fix), so `write(2)` returns EPIPE (swallowed by the `try?`) instead. Covers EVERY ProcessRunner consumer (jq, plugins, …). Added a DETERMINISTIC regression test (`ProcessRunnerTests.test_run_childExitsBeforeReadingStdin_doesNotSIGPIPE`: `/bin/sh -c 'exit 0'` + 1 MB stdin >> the 64 KB pipe buffer → merely reaching the assert proves no SIGPIPE; it would crash the test process pre-fix). Both it + `JQRunnerTests.test_invalid_filter_throws` pass; `swift build` green. Higher-value than another SRP slice — a user-facing crash fix surfaced by the gate flake. (TSK-1295, validated.)
- **[host] PluginSubprocessHost SIGPIPE class-fix (root-cause: "is this a CLASS of bugs?").** Grepped every subprocess stdin-write site after TSK-1295: `ProcessRunner` (fixed), `LSPClient` (already F_SETNOSIGPIPE-protected), AudioExporter/GitClient (`nullDevice` — no write), MCP (reads stdin) — and found **`PluginSubprocessHost`** writes the plugin envelope off-thread DIRECTLY (not via ProcessRunner), unprotected. A plugin that exits/crashes before draining a >64 KB envelope → SIGPIPE → host crash (same class). Fix: `fcntl(writeFD, F_SETNOSIGPIPE, 1)` (1 line, the proven pattern). Added a deterministic regression test (`PluginSubprocessHostTests.test_plugin_exits_before_reading_envelope_doesNotSIGPIPE`: a `#!/bin/sh; exit 0` plugin + a 200 KB envelope arg >> the 64 KB pipe buffer → reaching the assert proves no SIGPIPE; crashes the test process pre-fix). Passes; `swift build` green. The subprocess-stdin-write SIGPIPE class is now fully closed. (TSK-1296, validated.)

VALIDATION (per the riskiness directive — named, not deferred): host gate proves the model nonce + the JS mapping (FindCoordinatorTests: renderedScroll bumps+sets command, repeat-same still bumps, other bags untouched, scrollJS direction mapping w/ pageUp≠pageDown teeth); the real key event (field→onKeyPress→scroll) is AppKit-runtime → a VM/T4 key-routing UI test is the on-screen proof. ## LOG 2026-06-20 — editor scroll survives session/tab switch (warm-editor cache, TSK-1047)

Fixed the owner-reported **editor scroll resets on session AND tab switch** (the
rendered + read-only Source views already survived; only the CM6 editor lost it,
incl. the switch-tab → switch-session → return combo). Root cause confirmed: the
editor `WKWebView` was rebuilt on every switch (`makeNSView` builds /
`dismantleNSView` tears down), so CM6 reloaded at the top; the scroll-restore belt
(`seedEditorScroll` → `editorMountSelectionSeed` → `initialSelection`) lands on a
not-yet-laid-out fresh CM6 and effectively no-ops.

- **Cherry-picked TSK-1046** (`539eb8f0`, predecessor): the render-apply belt
  (`editorMountSelectionSeed` cursor-first-else-scroll-line; rendered no-reload
  re-apply) + the `ScrollRestoreUATTests` VM harness (verbs
  `editor-scroll-to-line`/`rendered-scroll-to`/`capture-rendered-scroll`,
  `editorScrollTopLine`/`renderedScrollY` dump fields, CM6 `scrollToLine`).
- **TSK-1047** — `WarmEditorWebViewCache` (sibling of `WarmWebViewCache`):
  path-keyed park-on-dismantle / re-attach-on-make so the editor WebView SURVIVES
  the switch (scroll preserved naturally, no reload). **Live/dirty-state guard
  (the crux):** an entry records the parked CM6's text; a re-attach is granted
  ONLY when the model's about-to-be-fed text matches byte-for-byte — else the
  parked editor is DROPPED and a fresh pane built against the model's text. So a
  re-attach can never resurrect stale text or mask unsaved edits (in-flight edits
  live in BOTH the parked JS and `editorBuffers`, so a genuine edit always
  matches; anything that would differ falls to the model-wins fresh build). Coord
  `adoptState` copies the `lastSent*` mirrors so `applyPendingState` no-ops the
  already-loaded doc (no `setText`/caret/scroll reset). Preview slot opts out (nil
  key) to keep its TSK-743/744 scroll-reset isolation.
- **Tests (teeth shown):** `WarmEditorWebViewCacheTests` (13) — round-trip,

## LOG 2026-06-18 — TSK-888 (slice): global-search per-file match-row cap (result-scroll perf)

888's typing side is ALREADY host-optimized — SearchAnywhereSection debounces 200ms + runs the search off-main
(Task.detached) + cancels in-flight (lines 346-357). The remaining result-SCROLL lag: the results LazyVStack
virtualizes FILE groups, but each fileGroup renders ALL of its file's matches eagerly (ForEach(file.matches.indices)),
each building a highlighted AttributedString — so a file with hundreds of matches makes that row + scrolling janky.
Fix: cap the rows rendered per file (pure ViewerCore SearchResultCap, default 50) + a "+N more in this file — open"
row that opens the file. Host teeth: SearchResultCapTests (3 — visible clamps to cap, overflow remainder, the cap
partitions with no loss). Bounds the worst-case per-file render; better UX too (no wall of matches). The common-case
scroll smoothness (many files, few matches each) is already lazy at the file level; any residual needs a scroll trace.

## LOG 2026-06-18 — TSK-887 (slice): command-palette `@`-mode heading re-parse memoized (first host-fixable P0)

The first cleanly HOST-FIXABLE P0 (the others were already-optimized or need lifecycle changes). CommandPaletteView's
`@` symbol mode re-parsed the WHOLE active file (MarkdownOutline.headings) on EVERY keystroke, though the parse is
query-independent (only the SymbolJump.rank below uses the query) — O(filesize) wasted per keystroke on a large file.
Fix: a tiny reusable ViewerCore `ParseMemo<Value>` (single-slot, String-keyed) memoizes the parse by file text →
parse once per file, rank per keystroke. Host teeth: ParseMemoTests (2 — recompute-only-on-key-change with a
call-count spy; empty-key validity). REMAINING (noted follow-on): the bare/file mode rebuilds `merged()` (bookmarks +
recents) per keystroke too — also query-independent; cache it on palette-open (smaller win than the heading parse).
887's full felt-validation (typing latency) is a VM/owner check; this removes a clear O(filesize)-per-keystroke waste.

## LOG 2026-06-18 — TSK-905: Markdown preview takes keyboard focus on activation (P1 bug; re-engaged per owner)

Owner pushback ("why so many no-ops? finish the curated tasks; if blocked, pick from the board") — I'd been
over-gating render-coupled P1 bugs as unshippable. Per the [VM] policy (build the model, host-test it, ship to
review), built TSK-905 (preview ↑/↓ dead unless the tab was the last one). Root cause: WKWebViews are
first-responder-by-tab-position — only the last-added one gets key events — so a non-last preview never
received arrows. Fix: a `previewFocusRequest` nonce on DocumentModel (mirrors 906's `editorFocusRequest`),
bumped from `updateDerived`'s new `refreshPreviewFocus()` ONLY when the active rendered-preview tab id CHANGES
(change-keyed → NO focus stealing on same-preview refreshes — the over-grab risk I'd flagged); MarkdownRenderedView
consumes it (Coordinator `lastFocusRequest` → `makeFirstResponder(webView)` in `updateNSView`), gated to the
ACTIVE tab in ContentView (`isActive ? model.previewFocusRequest : 0`). Host teeth: 2 new DocumentModelTests pin
bump-on-activation AND the no-regrab guard (the over-grab regression is now host-caught). Live scroll = VM tail
(review). Files: DocumentModel.swift, MarkdownRenderedView.swift, ContentView.swift, DocumentModelTests.swift.

## LOG 2026-06-18 — VM validation of the run (owner standing ask) → caught + fixed a flaky test

Ran the headless VM suite (`test-in-vm.sh test`, Swift 6.3) to validate this run's 9 accumulated items —

`TestTimingsTests.test_countsAllOutcomes` (my TSK-836 work). Cause: its `report()` helper read
`test-timings.py`'s stdout via a **Pipe**; under the VM's parallel load python hit a BrokenPipe at its at-exit
stdout flush → "Exception ignored in TextIOWrapper" → exit 120 → the `terminationStatus == 0` assertion failed
(+ 2 cascades). FIX: capture python's stdout to a **FILE** (a file can't break), mirroring the file-based
`JUnitConverterTests`. Host re-run 3/3 green. This is exactly why the VM-validation ask exists — the host's
lighter load never raced; the VM's parallelism did. Lesson recorded in LESSONS.md.

gate runs `swift test --parallel`, whose swiftpm progress reporter (`[N/M] Testing Class/method`) omits
per-case timing, and `--xunit-output` is broken on the host toolchain (writes no file). Only SERIAL
`swift test` emits the XCTest `Test Case … (N seconds).` lines the parser needs. Fixed `test-timings.sh` to
run serial + demonstrated a correct real report. The synthetic-fixture Swift test passed but the .sh fed the
wrong source — exactly the "demonstrate teeth on REAL data, not just a green fixture" lesson (now in LESSONS).
**Real measurement (serial, 5824 tests / 665 classes / 214s total) — the 849/850 targets:** the heaviest
classes cluster into two families. (1) GIT tests (per-method `git init` + ops): GitClientHistoryStatsTests
8.8s, RepoFocusTrackerTests 7.3s, GitLogStalePageGuardTests 7.3s (3637 ms/test!), GitClient*/GitLog*/
CommitReview*/Cumulative*/GitPanel* — collectively the biggest bucket → TSK-850 (share an immutable git
fixture across the class). (2) SLEEP/WAIT tests: FolderWatcherTests 6.9s, LSPClientSmokeTests 3245 ms/1 test,
LSPPoolSmokeTests 2131 ms/test, GrandchildPipeTests 2908 ms/test, ModeSwitchRaceTests → TSK-849 (replace
fixed sleeps with condition-waits). High avg-ms/test classes block a parallel worker longest, so they're the
priority. Full top-25 in the commit's run; `bash scripts/test-timings.sh` reproduces.

## LOG 2026-06-15 — TSK-953: fixed the VM GUI-lane UAT harness (53 false reds → real signal)

VM back. Owner directive "fix the UAT harness first" — the GUI lane (`MDV_VM_GUI_SESSION=1`) was reporting
~53 live-app UAT failures that were a HARNESS artifact, not product regressions (headless = 0 on the same
code). Root-caused, fixed, verified red→green, gate-green, committed.

**Root cause (one cause, many symptoms).** The `sudo launchctl asuser <consoleUID> /bin/bash` bridge runs
xctest as ROOT (EUID 0) while `AppLauncher` spawns the live app as the console user (required for
WindowServer key/activation, TSK-620). xctest's `FileManager.temporaryDirectory` resolves by EUID to
ROOT's `/var/folders/zz/.../T` (0700) — untraversable by the console-user app → fixtures `.error`, and
everything downstream (editor-save round-trips, sidebar root, bookmark persistence) fails.

**Two dead-ends ruled out by direct VM instrumentation (probed through the exact asuser bridge):**
(1) you CANNOT `chmod` root's temp open — `/var/folders/.../T` is SIP-restricted (`SF_RESTRICTED`), EUID-0
chmod = `Operation not permitted`; (2) `FileManager.temporaryDirectory` ignores `$TMPDIR` (uses
`confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)`), so the earlier TMPDIR-redirect was a no-op. Reverted the dead
`test-in-vm.sh` chmod.

**Fix (in-place, one mechanism).** `LaunchHarness` roots fixtures under the spawn user's HOME
(`AppLauncher.spawnUserHome/.mdv-uat-fixtures`) when `geteuid()==0`; `AppLauncher.runScript` gained
`preShared` → skips its copy-to-/tmp indirection, `chown -R`s the run dir to the console user, runs the app
against the REAL stable paths, and does NOT reap the dir between a method's scenarios. The replaced copy
indirection itself broke editor-save round-trips (app saved a copy the test never read back) and
multi-launch path-keyed bookmarks (new uuid path per launch). Files:
`Tests/ViewerUITests/AppLauncher.swift`, `Tests/ViewerUITests/Harness/LaunchHarness.swift`,
`scripts/test-in-vm.sh`.

**TSK-954 (found by the full GUI `all` lane) — partial; PMA needs a follow-on.** An initial cut used `/tmp`;
the full lane then showed 19 failures, ALL in `PluginsAndMcpAutomationUATTests` — the MCP `open_path`
containment fence (`MCPToolCatalog`) admits a path only if it's under the MCP SERVER process's home or that
process's own per-user temp. Moving the fixture base from `/tmp` to `spawnUserHome/.mdv-uat-fixtures` kept
Cm6/Sidebar green (file-UAT app = console user, home = `/Users/vm-tester`), killed the `.error` class and the
`-609` connection errors, and cut PMA 19→16 — BUT did not green PMA. ROOT CAUSE of the remainder:
`MCPClient` (in the PMA test) spawns `--mcp-stdio` DIRECTLY as ROOT (no `sudo -u`), so the server's
`NSHomeDirectory()` is `/var/root`, not `/Users/vm-tester` — the home-based fixtures are "outside" the
server's home → rejected. The file-UAT app (console user) and the MCP server (root) have DIFFERENT homes,
so no single fixture base satisfies both while they run as different users. COMPLETE FIX (follow-on, owner
paused the loop so HELD): make `MCPClient` spawn the server as the console user too (mirror AppLauncher),
so both lanes are the console user and share `/Users/vm-tester`. The home-base fixture change is committed as
the correct foundation; PMA stays red pending the MCPClient-spawn fix. Host gate green (PMA self-skips on
host); Cm6/Sidebar 10/10 on the VM.

**Validation (teeth demonstrated).** Same two worst classes (`Cm6EditorUATTests` +
`SidebarFileTreeAndBookmarksUATTests`): **31 failures on the broken harness → 0 failures, 20/20, `.error`=0**
on the fixed harness (VM GUI lane, fresh test target). Host headless gate: PASS (5813 tests, tier
enforcement OK). Next: full GUI `all` lane vs fresh `dist/` for the complete render signal, then drain the
~99-item `review` pile.

## LOG 2026-06-15 — TSK-952 flaky perf benches (single-sample → best-of-N) (→ review)

VM still down (3rd tick — `ssh macOS15` timeout), host feature pool scraped, review pile correctly
VM/owner-gated (self-validating those would over-claim the render). Rather than repeat the HOLD or
manufacture a marginal VM-tail slice, fixed a CONCRETE, host-validatable, recurring problem: the perf
benches that flake the gate under load (bitten 4+ times this session, always bench-only — which masks
real reds and wastes re-runs on the owner's velocity bottleneck).

Root cause: each bench took a SINGLE wall-clock sample, then asserted a threshold — a scheduler/GC spike
on that one sample flaked it. Fix (TSK-952): take the BEST (min) of N runs per measurement. The minimum
is the least load-contaminated estimate of true compute cost (load only ADDS time), so this kills the
single-sample flakiness WITHOUT loosening any threshold — a genuine regression slows EVERY run including
the min, so the teeth survive.
- `CrossFileSearchBenchTests` (per-line substring-reject ratio): best-of-5 → stable 1.007x (was flaking
  at 0.66x under load). Self-contained inline micro-bench (NOT the CrossFileSearch engine) → §2.5-irrelevant.
- `FoldBenchTests`: cold-compute best-of-3 (<250ms), warm-cache best-of-5 (<5ms — the most spike-prone,
  a single sample at a 5ms threshold flaked on one hiccup).
- Left alone (not flaky): HexDumpBuilder microbench (500ms threshold = ~100x headroom), TextFileLoaderBench
  (prints only, no time assert).

Test-only change (no Sources/ touched) — not user-facing, so no CHANGELOG line. Targeted benches pass
(stable numbers logged); headless gate green. Validated on the host (the change IS test-harness logic,
fully host-exercised). → review.

## LOG 2026-06-15 — TSK-901 content auto-detect for misnamed JSON/CSV files (→ review)

The JSON/CSV menu tools gated purely on extension (`canMinifyActiveJSON` → `.json`,
`canConvertActiveCSV` → `.csv`/`.tsv`), so a misnamed file (e.g. `data.txt` holding JSON) got no
tools — exactly the TSK-901 gap. Fixed WITHOUT a FileCategory/type-system change (which the earlier
spike flagged as the heavy path): a conservative content sniffer feeding the existing tool gates.

New `ViewerCore.ContentTypeSniffer` (pure, host-tested): `detect(_:) -> .json | .csv | nil`. JSON =
leading `{`/`[` AND a real `JSONSerialization` parse (so `[TODO] note` / `{ a note }` are rejected);
CSV = the first ≤5 non-empty lines share a consistent `,`/`\t` delimiter with ≥2 fields and ≥2 rows
(rejects prose-with-commas + single-column word lists). STRICT by design — a false positive (prose→data)
is worse than a miss (worst case: a tool stays menu-disabled). `DocumentModel.canMinifyActiveJSON` /
`canConvertActiveCSV` now fall back to `sniffedActiveContentKind()` when the extension doesn't match —
size-capped at 1 MiB so the menu-validate path stays cheap (beyond the cap, extension-only).

Teeth: 12 `ContentTypeSnifferTests` (JSON object/array/whitespace-led/invalid-bracket/prose; CSV
consistent/tab/inconsistent/single-col/single-row/empty; multiline-JSON-not-CSV) + 4 `DocumentModelTests`
(misnamed `.txt` JSON → JSON tools enabled; misnamed `.txt` CSV → CSV tools enabled; prose → both
disabled; real `.json` fast-path unchanged). Headless gate green; no exe change (menu items already
gate on these properties). § note: builds a new sniffer + extends CONSUMER gates — does not touch the
ported CSV engine (§2.5-safe). The "language" half of 901 (highlight a misnamed code file) is deferred
(needs the TreeSitter language-map keyed off content — a separate slice). → review.

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-946 + TSK-949 find-menu bugs from the parity audit (→ review)

Drained the two host-fixable find-menu bugs the TSK-939 audit surfaced (B4 + B6).

**TSK-946 (B4) — Find Next/Prev (⌘G/⌥⌘G) were inert.** The menu items targeted
`NSTextView.performFindPanelAction` with NSTextFinder tags, but no surface sets `usesFindBar`
(our find bars are custom `FindCoordinator` bags) — so ⌘G/⌥⌘G did nothing; next/prev was only
Return/Shift-Return inside the open bar. Fix: added `FindCoordinator.next()/prev()` — a router
that bumps the OPEN bar's existing next/prev request nonce (editor → rendered → source order,
mutually exclusive in practice), plus `isAnyBarPresented`. Forwarded as `DocumentModel.findNext()/
findPrev()` + `canFindNextPrev`. Retargeted the menu items to new `@objc findNextInPage/
findPrevInPage` handlers (target self) + a `validateMenuItem` gate (grey when no bar open).

**TSK-949 (B6) — ⌥⌘F wasn't greyed outside the editor.** `replaceInPage` silently degraded to
plain Find on the read-only rendered/source views — a surprise (Find&Replace looks available, only
gives Find). Fix: added `DocumentModel.canFindAndReplace` (`tabs.selected != nil &&
currentViewMode == .editor`) + a `validateMenuItem` case so ⌥⌘F greys outside the editor;
simplified the handler to editor-only (dropped the degrade-to-find fallback).

Teeth (host): 7 new `FindCoordinatorTests` (router routes to each open bar; no-op when none open;
editor-wins-when-multiple; `isAnyBarPresented` tracks state) + 4 `DocumentModelTests`
(`canFindAndReplace` false/no-tab, true/editor, false/source; `canFindNextPrev` follows the open
bar). Headless gate green. The on-screen ⌘G stepping + the greyed menu item are render/first-
responder behavior → VM tail. Both → review.

framework, not a third-party dep) in a fresh JSContext SANDBOX — pure ECMAScript, no fetch/require/process/FS/DOM,
so a transform reshapes in-memory JSON but can't do I/O. Slices: (1) engine [DONE], (2) safe off-main exec + soft

JSContext, evals the expression, returns `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)`; distinct errors for invalidJSON /
jsException / unserializableResult. Teeth: 13 host tests incl. map/filter/reduce, property access, errors, and
SANDBOX teeth (`typeof fetch|require|process === "undefined"`). JavaScriptCore auto-links (no Package.swift
change). Host gate green. No CHANGELOG (no user-visible surface yet — engine foundation only).

OWNER NOTE: engine runs sandboxed arbitrary JS per the explicit "JS-type" ask; if a safer JQ-subset is preferred,
that's a one-word redirect.

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-929 follow external rename → update tab (→ review)

A single-file watcher learns a file vanished from its path but not where it went (kqueue gives no new name). Fix:
capture the watched file's INODE at watch-start; on the watcher tick, if the file is gone at its path, scan the
parent folder for that inode (new `RenameFollower.findRenamed` / `inode(of:)`, ViewerCore, FS-based + host-tested)
and, if found, follow the rename — set `tab.url` to the new path, mark `.fresh`, re-point the watcher (re-captures
inode), and reload — instead of `refreshDiskState` → `.deleted` ("file not found"). Safe because editor buffer +
scroll/cursor are tab.id-keyed (TSK-718), so they follow the tab across the URL change; URL-keyed secondary state
(bookmarks/recents) is a minor edge, noted. A true delete or a move OUT of the folder still reports gone.

Teeth: 5 host tests on real temp-dir renames (finds renamed by inode; true-delete→nil; moved-out→nil;
distinct-file-same-folder not mis-matched; inode-of-missing→nil). Host gate green. The live watcher-event path
(DispatchSource rename tick → follow) is integration/VM; the follow DECISION + inode match are host-pinned.

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-903 markdown task-list checkboxes (cross-engine, → review)

Executed the triaged TSK-903 slice (deferred twice; done now). Both markdown engines deliberately dropped GFM
task-list markers; now they emit a disabled checkbox. KEY SIMPLIFICATION found during impl: the checkbox is

  — both engines now produce identical checkbox HTML, so parity holds (verified: 6/6 A/B tests pass).
- **CSS (markdown.css):** `:has()` rules drop the bullet for task items + dim/strike completed ones (WebKit 15.4+,
  available in the app's WKWebView; degrades to bullet+checkbox without `:has`).

Validated: rebuilt libmdvcore_ffi.a (build-rust-core.sh) → **rust-core gate green** + **swift headless gate** +

Root-caused the owner's "plain-text identified but locked in HEX" bug. The SYNC open path passes the loader's
text/binary verdict into mode resolution (TSK-332), so small unknown-extension text files open in `.source`
correctly. But the DEFERRED off-main path (files ≥4 MiB, TSK-842 `deferReadOffMainBytes`) resolves the mode
BEFORE reading bytes → `isRenderableText: nil` → unknown extension gets the hint-less `.hex` default. On load
completion (`openLargeFileOffMain`), the "carry HEX" block then called `loadBinaryAsync` for a `.loaded` (TEXT!)
file — dumping a text file as hex while the picker re-derived to offer Source (the exact desync).

Fix: new pure `DocumentModel.deferredLoadViewModeUpgrade(current:isLoadedText:url:preferred:)` — a `.hex` tab that
decoded as text upgrades to the content-aware default (`ViewModeOptions.defaultMode` with the hint); non-hex tabs
and non-text (`.binary`/`.error`/…) states are untouched, so a genuinely binary file stays HEX. Wired into the
off-main completion before the carry block (so a text file never reaches `loadBinaryAsync`). Safe because the
deferred path is the plain `open(url:)` only — explicit "Open As HEX" goes through the sync forced-category path,
never here. Teeth: 4 host tests (unknown-text→Source, binary→stays-HEX, non-hex-unchanged, never-HEX-for-text).

SIBLING NOTED (not touched): the `materializeIfNeeded` carry block (DocumentModel.swift:5685) has the same shape
but carries a PERSISTED mode (could be a user's explicit Open-As-HEX), so upgrading there risks clobbering intent
— left as a separate follow-up if the session-restore case surfaces. Host gate green.

## LOG 2026-06-14 — Check Links shipped (TSK-867, c2cabbb, → review)

Third consecutive §2.5-safe markdown feature (TOC → HTML export → Check Links), all found by probing for
consumer/output features rather than HOLDing. **View ▸ Check Links** reports broken LOCAL links/images in the
active Markdown — a real docs-maintenance win (the owner writes a lot of markdown docs with cross-references).

- **MarkdownLinks** (pure, ViewerCore): `extract` finds inline `[text](url)` + image `![alt](url)` links via a
  line-walk that skips fenced code, handles nested brackets (link text) + nested parens (URL) + backslash escapes,
  and drops the optional `"title"`. `kind(of:)` classifies external (scheme/`//`) / anchor (`#`) / relative.
  `brokenLocalLinks(in:exists:)` returns relative links whose target (with any `#fragment` stripped) fails the
  INJECTED `exists` closure — so the whole checker is host-testable with no real filesystem. A focused parser like
  `MarkdownOutline` (not the ported markdown→HTML engine) → §2.5-safe.
- **DocumentModel.checkLinksInActiveMarkdown()** resolves relative targets (percent-decoded) against the file's
  directory + `FileManager.fileExists`; returns total + broken. `Edit`… actually `View ▸ Check Links` → NSAlert
  ("All links OK / N of M broken" + the broken list with line numbers).

v1 limits (documented): reference-style links + links inside inline-code spans aren't parsed. Teeth: 8 pure tests
(extract incl. fenced-skip + nested + title-drop, kind classification, broken-relative-only via injected exists,
#fragment strip). Host gate green (5553 tests). Menu + alert = VM tail. Filed standalone (TSK-867).

## LOG 2026-06-14 — Copy/Export as HTML shipped (TSK-866, 5c95a23, → review)

Kept applying the "§2.5-safe CONSUMER features still exist" lesson — shipped a high-value, commonly-wanted
markdown export. **View ▸ Copy as HTML / Export as HTML…** renders the active Markdown to a STANDALONE HTML
document.

Key insight (gives it real host teeth): `HTMLRenderer.renderPage` (the in-app WKWebView page) carries a strict
no-network **CSP** — correct for the sandboxed viewer, but it would BLOCK external images/fonts when the user
opens the exported file in a browser. So export needs a DIFFERENT assembly: new pure `HtmlExport.standaloneDocument`
(ViewerCore) wraps `HTMLRenderer.render(text)` (the body) + the bundled stylesheet + theme overrides into a
complete `<!DOCTYPE html>` doc **without** the CSP. `DocumentModel.htmlExportForActiveMarkdown()` self-assembles
(HTMLRenderer() + MarkdownStylesheet.load() + themedExtraStylesheet — no ContentView coupling). Copy → NSPasteboard;
Export → NSSavePanel (default `<stem>.html`). Markdown files only.

§2.5: a CONSUMER (calls the Rust-routed `render`, builds a new wrapper) — not an engine modification. Safe.

Teeth: 4 pure `HtmlExportTests` — body/stylesheet/charset embedded, `<title>` HTML-escaped, **NO
Content-Security-Policy** (pins the load-bearing export-vs-in-app distinction; a regression routing export through
the CSP'd page fails), filename `.ext` swap. Host gate green (5545 tests). Menu + clipboard/save-panel = VM tail.
Filed standalone (TSK-866) — it's a markdown-app export, not part of the 675 editor epic.

  heading present, `[`/`]` escaped in link text. `insert(into:headings:)` is IDEMPOTENT via `<!-- toc -->` /
  `<!-- /toc -->` markers (re-run regenerates the block in place, never stacks) and inserts after a leading YAML
  front-matter block when present. `DocumentModel.insertTableOfContents()` runs it through the shared
  encoding-preserving write-through; `Edit ▸ Insert Table of Contents` is gated to Markdown files.

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-675 slice 4 shipped: Convert Indentation (Tabs↔Spaces) (2a8b111, → review)

Drained the last clean host-buildable robust-editor command from the 675 runway. Child TSK-864 → review.

- **Convert Indentation** (Edit ▸ Convert Indentation ▸ {Tabs → Spaces, Spaces → Tabs}): `IndentConverter`
  (ViewerCore, pure, scalar-walk) rewrites ONLY each line's leading-whitespace run — tabs→spaces (each tab →
  `width` spaces) / spaces→tabs (each `width`-run → one tab, partial run kept; existing leading tabs flush pending
  spaces then pass through) — leaving post-content alignment + line terminators (LF/CRLF/CR) byte-intact. Driven
  through the shared `applyTextTransformToActiveFile` helper (encoding-preserving), width from `CMIndentation.size`.
  Indent DETECTION is Rust-ported (`RustIndentAdapter`); this conversion is a new transform (not the detector twin),
  so §2.5-clean.

Teeth: 10 pure tests (leading-only, non-leading untouched, CRLF preserved, partial runs, **round-trip
spaces↔tabs**, empty). Host gate green (5529 tests, tier OK). Menu render = VM tail.

675 now has 4 slices at review (862 line-endings; 863 cleanup+stats; 864 indentation). **The clean HOST-buildable
robust-editor command runway is ~drained** — remaining 675 work is render/CM6-coupled (line ops duplicate/move/

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-675 slices 2+3 shipped: Document Statistics + Whitespace cleanup (90196d2, → review)

Continued draining the P0 epic's host-buildable runway (the payoff of unblocking it last firing). Batched two
independent slices, gated once, child TSK-863 → review:

- **Trim Trailing Whitespace + Ensure Final Newline** (Edit menu): `TextCleanup` (ViewerCore, pure, scalar-walk) —
  KEY distinction from the existing `TextTools.trimTrailingWhitespace` (a TSK-352 *clipboard* tool that rejoins
  with `\n`, CRLF-lossy): the file commands PRESERVE each line's terminator byte-for-byte (converting line endings
  as a side effect of "trim whitespace" would be silent data loss). `DocumentModel` applies them via a new shared
  `applyTextTransformToActiveFile` helper (encoding-preserving write-through + drop/reload, the Convert-Encoding
  mechanism; reusable for future text commands). `ensureFinalNewline` matches the file's dominant ending.
- **Document Statistics** (View ▸ Document Statistics → info alert): `DocumentStats.compute` — CRLF-aware line
  count (trailing newline not double-counted, `\r\n` = one break), whitespace-collapsed word count, grapheme-correct
  characters (`café 🌟` = 6) + a no-whitespace count. Menu→`NSAlert` on demand (no per-keystroke cost).

Teeth: 16 pure tests (9 TextCleanup incl. CRLF/lone-CR terminator preservation + blank-line handling; 7
DocumentStats incl. line-count edge cases + multibyte). Host gate green (5519 tests, tier OK). Menus + alert = VM tail.

675 now has 3 slices shipped (862 line-endings; 863 cleanup+stats). REMAINING is render-coupled CM6 (line ops:
duplicate/move/delete; column/block select; macro record-replay; insert/overwrite; optional auto-cleanup-on-save) —
VM/later. Commit note: both slices interleave in DocumentModel/main, so they landed as one gated commit (90196d2)
rather than two (clean per-hunk split needs interactive staging).

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-533 audio frequency-spectrum panel SHIPPED (fb2ada6, → review)

Built the first item off last firing's mapped niche tail, and **corrected last firing's own blocker**:
the prior sweep called 533 "not a clean leaf — the viewModel keeps PEAKS, not the float buffer." That was
wrong — `AudioWaveform.samples` holds the **full** deinterleaved mono buffer ("Held in full" — kept exactly
so the view can re-reduce per zoom without re-decoding). So the FFT can read `samples` directly; 533 *was* a
clean additive leaf.

What shipped (commit `fb2ada6`):
- **Pure model** (`AudioWaveform`, host-tested): `spectrumWindow(centeredOn:fftSize:)` extracts a playhead-
  centred, buffer-clamped window (clamps at both edges; whole buffer when shorter than the FFT; empty when
  empty); `spectrum(at:)` runs the existing host-tested `SpectrumAnalyzer`. `SpectrumBins` now carries
  `floorDB` so the renderer normalises `[floorDB,0]→[0,1]` without a magic constant (only `analyze`
  constructs it; tests use `analyze()`, so no breakage).
- **View model** (`AudioEditorViewModel`): `showSpectrum` toggle + a playhead-tracking `spectrum`, recomputed
  on the playback tick / scrub **while shown** (a 2048-pt FFT is cheap; gated so a hidden panel does no work)
  and cleared when hidden. Added a `init(url:waveform:)` test seam.
- **View** (`AudioEditorView`): a spectrum toggle button (`mdv.audioEditor.spectrumToggle`) + a linear-
  frequency `spectrumCanvas` panel (`mdv.audioEditor.spectrum`) that drops in below the waveform. Pure SwiftUI
  `Canvas` like the waveform — no `NSViewRepresentable`, so the sibling-blank occlusion class can't apply.

Teeth: 8 new pure tests (window centring via a ramp buffer where `samples[i]==i`, start/end clamp, short/empty
buffer, sine→peak-bin composition, floorDB carry) + 4 new VM tests (toggle on→spectrum present, off→cleared,
scrub-recompute gated on `showSpectrum`). Host headless gate green (5484 tests, tier enforcement OK). On-screen
Canvas render is the VM tail (extend `AudioEditorVisualRegressionTests` T5 to cover the spectrum band).

Batch note: shipped ONE complete item this firing rather than forcing a marginal second. The remaining queue tail
is render-only (766 git-diff style / 506 treemap — no host model → blind = the risky-change the owner warned off),
owner-gated (343/358), or VM-heavy investigations (668 CSV paging, 463/710/708 LSP bridges, 839 trace, 838 arch) —
none a clean fold-in. 534 (trim/fade) is now more attractive: `AudioExporter`/`AudioDocument` exist, so trim/fade
could feed a real "Save a Copy" → a complete feature next firing.

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-829 SHIPPED: parallel cross-file search, 4.7× (validated) — broke the defer pattern

Committed to building the SPEED win this firing (after 3 design/triage firings). Implemented the finalized design
with the TSK-847 measurement discipline.

- **TSK-829 [perf, VALIDATED @ `a3ca530`]** — cross-file search (`CrossFileSearch.search`) now matches files in
  PARALLEL. The serial walk (dir-skip + symlink-loop guard + caps + cancellation) is unchanged and collects
  candidate URLs into batches of 24; each batch is matched via `DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform` into per-index
  slots (`withUnsafeMutableBufferPointer` + `nonisolated(unsafe)` base pointer — disjoint writes, race-free; the
  heavy read+decode+match moved into a new `matchFile`; `Matcher` is `@unchecked Sendable` — its closures only read
  a thread-safe `NSRegularExpression` / pure `String.range`); then folded SERIALLY in walk order under the global
  `maxResults` gate (reproduces the old loop's mid-file cap break exactly). Over-read bounded to one batch — the
  key to NOT regressing common-term searches (the `maxResults=500` early-break the naive two-phase would have
  defeated, per last firing's finding).
- **MEASURED 4.7×** (TSK-847 discipline): serial baseline 585.7 ms → parallel 123.7 ms on a 3000-file × 40-line
  synthetic corpus, IDENTICAL 21000 matches both. Env-gated bench (no flaky wall-clock gate assert).
- **Validated:** correctness is regression-guarded — a concurrency bug would produce wrong/missing/misordered
  results and fail the +3 new parity tests (mid-file cap, line order, all-50-files-found) AND the existing
  CrossFileSearch/CrossSearch suites (the broad parity guard) — and the design is race-free BY CONSTRUCTION
  (concurrentPerform is a barrier; disjoint per-index writes; serial fold). Headless gate green. CHANGELOG entry
  added (Performance — user-felt search latency).

## LOG 2026-06-14 — TSK-861 (UTF-16 BOM data-fidelity bug, validated) + TSK-855 (stale-serve gate fix, review) — batched, one gate

Fresh firing. Two newly-filed board bugs (not in WORK_QUEUE) pre-empted the queue per rank rule 1 (user-facing
bug) + rule 2 (test-infra correctness). Batched, gated ONCE, committed separately.

- **TSK-861 [bug, user-facing, validated `e7a5649`]** — `EditorWriter.save` wrote `text.data(using: encoding)`;
  for `.utf16LittleEndian`/`.utf16BigEndian` (the encodings `TextDecoder.decodeViaBOM` records *after stripping
  the BOM on read*) that produces BOM-LESS bytes. On reopen a SHORT UTF-16 file fails the read side's ≥32-byte
  BOM-less heuristic → mis-decodes as CP1252/Latin-1 (garbled) — or, with the fix disabled, `binaryFile`.
  Reachable from the editor's own save (`EditorCoordinator:499` uses `buf.encoding`) AND CrossFileReplace; Convert
  Encoding's "UTF-16" uses BOM-ful `.utf16` so it was already safe. Centralized fix: `EditorWriter.withByteOrderMark`
  prepends FF FE / FE FF for the explicit-endianness cases (`.utf16`/`.unicode` already BOM-ful; UTF-8/CP1252/
  Latin-1 untouched). 7 host tests (LE+BE short-file open→edit→save→reopen round-trip, BOM-byte check, helper
  unit cases, UTF-8-stays-BOM-less); TEETH: disabling the re-emission makes the round-trip decode as `binaryFile`.
  Self-validated (pure ViewerCore logic). CHANGELOG Fixed entry added.
- **TSK-855 [CI/test-infra bug, review `96851a1`]** — `RemoteTransportLoopbackTests` spawns the real `mdv-serve`
  to prove engine surface byte-equal local-FFI vs remote, but `build-rust-core.sh` builds ONLY the dist FFI
  staticlib, never the serve bin — so the suite ran against a possibly days-stale `mdv-serve` (false RED on the
  TSK-841 wire change; worse, a false PASS for a non-decode-breaking wire change, defeating the loopback's point).
  Fix (option c): `test-headless-gate.sh` now `cargo build -p mdvcore-serve` fresh into the exact debug path the
  test resolves, before `swift test`, guarded on `command -v cargo` (VM/no-cargo hosts keep self-skipping).
  Verified in THIS gate run: the serve build ran + `test_engineSurface_byteEqual_localVsRemote` executed (not
  skipped) green. Left at `review` (the gate-builds-serve behavior isn't tightly regression-guarded — a removal
  surfaces only on a future wire change; optional follow-up: an mtime staleness assertion in the test).
- **Gate:** single `scripts/test-headless-gate.sh` run, PASSED (5429 tests, no heavy tier), validating both.

double-allocation** fix. The heap cap is the pre-existing TSK-557 guard, which the new path PRESERVES untouched.

- **What it was:** `CsvSession::open` built a `Vec<Vec<String>>` (one heap `String`/cell via `mem::take`), then
  `TableArena::from_table` copied every cell's bytes into the contiguous arena and freed the Vec. For a 1M-cell
  file: ~2M allocations + a full second byte-copy. (Ticket measured 140 ms open.)
- **Fix (commit `3d75f39`):** refactored the SINGLE CSV tokenizer to drive a `CsvSink` trait. `VecSink` keeps the
  wire `Vec<Vec<String>>` DTO path (TUI/web table View, `csv::parse`); new `ArenaSink` writes cell bytes STRAIGHT
  into the arena buffer with a **reused** field scratch (`field.clear()` not `mem::take`) — no per-cell `String`,
  no second copy. `CsvSession::open` → `csv::parse_arena`. Fast path: when rows are at header arity the as-built
  buffer IS the arena (zero extra copies); ragged rows take a one-copy normalization pass.
- **Correctness by construction:** ALL resource-cap accounting (cell-chars/…-marker, input-scalars, total-cells,
  cells-per-row, estimated-heap) stays in the shared tokenizer, so both sinks see byte-identical caps.
- **Refereed:** 5 parity tests (logical-table over the golden corpus incl ragged/CRLF/quoted/unicode/terminal-
  drop; byte-identical arena for well-formed; cap parity ×5; heap-flood cap parity; 5k-row scale) + the 23 golden
  csv tests = 28/28 green. **TEETH:** disabling `ArenaSink` terminal-drop made the parity guard FAIL (diverged on
  `\n` + heap-flood); restored → green. FFI surface unchanged (header-drift clean), wire output byte-identical.
- **Validated:** `scripts/rust-core-gate.sh` green on the committed commit (build + workspace tests + clippy
  deny-lints + header-drift). TSK-844 → `validated` (agent self-validation: pure host-testable parser logic with
  teeth-demonstrated regression tests). CHANGELOG Performance entry added.

**Rust-core lane status update:** 575 cast-safety DONE; **844 CSV-arena DONE (this firing)**; 564 FFI double-copy
= ~12-site fresh-session refactor still scoped/pending; 573 web last-resort. Strategic state otherwise unchanged
(Swift queue drained, snippets model done, 382 needs a VM profile, owner 343/358 + the VM review lane outstanding).

  F2-already-sidebar-rename, code-actions ⌘.-is-Mac-Cancel, sidebar ⌘B-vs-existing-⌃⌘S) flagged in the doc
  for an owner pick, NOT imposed. Host-tested via shortcutMap.
- **TSK-350 (`8449333`, review)** — markdown pipe-table alignment. Pure `Formatter.prettyPrintMarkdown`
  (column pad, :--/:-:/--: alignment, escaped-pipe + fenced-code aware) surfaced as an in-place **Align
  Markdown Tables** Edit-menu command (rewrites the active editor buffer). Host-tested (FormatterTests +
  MarkdownTableFormatModelTests).

**Design wall caught by the gate (important):** my first cut added `.md` to `Formatter.SupportedFormat.detect`.
The gate failed `FormatToggleTests.test_markdownFile_doesNotSupportFormatToggle` — `detect` gates the format
VIEW lens (`.formatted`) + the Format toggle, and **markdown deliberately has NO format mode** (its lenses are
Rendered/Source). There's a DUAL gate: `Formatter.detect` → `supportsFormatToggle`; a SEPARATE
`ViewMode.formatterExtensions` → the `.formatted` mode — md is intentionally in neither, and they must agree
(else the Format button toggles to a `.formatted` mode absent from the picker). So the view-lens path is
correctly closed for md; I reworked to surface alignment as an in-place COMMAND instead (detect stays md-free).
Lesson: a change to `Formatter.detect` is a VIEW-MODE change, not just a formatter change — check the dual gate.

**TSK-350 spike finding:** the other `detect()` absences (.jsonl/.svg/.scss/.less/.jsx/.ts) are DELIBERATE,
documented exclusions (the lexers can't safely model them) — so there's no further clean detect()-gap; new
format types (YAML/TOML/SQL) would each be a from-scratch dependency-free formatter (own ticket if wanted).

**Gate caught a real bug** before commit: Swift merges `\r\n` into a SINGLE `Character` grapheme cluster,
so my `text[i] == "\n"` line scan never fired on CRLF files (returned the whole file as line 1). Fixed to
`Character.isNewline` (covers `\n`, `\r\n`, lone `\r`, Unicode separators). Re-gated green, then committed.

**Why one item this firing (not the cron's 2-3):** the other next-queue items are render-coupled in a way

## Validation methods available (no owner staring required)
- **Headless gate** (window-free): `bash scripts/test-headless-gate.sh` → exit 0 + "tier enforcement OK". The merge gate.
- **`--diagnose`**: `MDV_BACKGROUND=1 .build/debug/MarkdownViewer --diagnose [-MarkdownViewer.<key> <val>] <file>` → JSON view tree (frames + classes). Confirms which view mounts / layout geometry. Window-free-ish (brief offscreen).
- **Live footprint**: launch debug binary bg → `footprint <pid>` (phys_footprint), `vmmap -summary <pid>`, `pgrep`-by-ppid for child procs. Screen is ours.
- **Self-read screenshots**: `screencapture -x -o /tmp/x.png` then Read the PNG. (System-wide capture — note the owner's other windows; don't comment on them.)
- **Perf timing**: instrument with signposts / wall-clock logs to stderr, parse from the log.

## LOG 2026-06-09 (latest+106) — FIXED: TSK-507 PluginSubprocessHost gate-flake → done (teeth: suite green + kill-path intact)

- **TSK-507** ([test][flaky] PluginSubprocessHostTests false-red under load) → **done** (commit `cac7227`). Root cause: the
  immediate-echo fixture scripts passed a tight `timeoutMs:3000` to `host.call`; on a saturated runner the child is
  CPU-starved and the 3s per-call deadline elapses before it completes → host terminates it → timeout outcome → XCTFail
  (`test_happy_path`/`test_nonzero_exit` observed at ~8.4s on 2026-06-08, cost a gate re-run). Fix: a single documented
  `safeTimeoutMs = 15_000` constant replaces every immediate-echo case's `3000` (14 sites) — it's a **ceiling, not a
  sleep**, so zero cost on a healthy run (echo finishes in ms); 15s < host `maxTimeoutMs`(30s) so no clamp.
  `test_timeout_kills_runaway` KEEPS its deliberate `200ms` budget. Verified: full suite **21/21** green in 5.3s incl.
  the kill-path test (0.49s — the SIGTERM/SIGKILL mechanism still fires, so the bump didn't neuter the timeout). This is
  the exact flake that's intermittently reddened my own headless-gate runs — it improves merge-gate reliability.

- Re-verified (fresh) the SwiftUI + PORT lanes are genuinely owner-gated: `task_list waiting=human` = TSK-250 (web

  (`.loaded` ⇒ true; every other state ⇒ nil, leaving the extension default). Factored the carry-mode logic out of
  `openResolved`'s inline closure into `resolveOpenMode(_:forceNewTab:isRenderableText:)` so BOTH the default and the
  carry-membership check honor the hint. `openResolved` now resolves the mode AFTER the sync load and threads
  `renderableTextHint(state)`; `availableViewModes` threads it from `tabs.selected?.state`. The off-main large-file
  path resolves un-hinted (no sync read) and self-corrects via `availableViewModes` once the async load lands
  `.loaded`. The lazy/session-restore append (`.empty` state) correctly passes no hint.

  offers `[Source,HEX]`; a NUL-byte `.xyzzy` stays `.hex`-only (content-driven, not blanket unknown→source); the
  state→hint derivation. **Demoed red** (suppress the hint → opens HEX). Headless gate green on the committed tree.

## LOG 2026-06-09 (latest+88) — TSK-257 + TSK-258 VALIDATED: syntax highlighting COMPLETE (full 12-grammar set)

Increment 4 landed (commit `1590bf8`): `mdvcore-highlight` now carries the **full owner-approved grammar set** —
json, rust, javascript, typescript, tsx, java, c, cpp, c-sharp, swift, kotlin, lua (12 `Lang` variants). Both
rust-core front-ends (TUI + web) light up source views for all of them. **Both board tasks now `validated`** on

- **Three tree-sitter nuances solved** (each cost a red build first):
  - **`; inherits:` is NOT auto-resolved by tree-sitter-highlight.** TS/TSX `; inherits: javascript` and C++
    `; inherits: c` only ship the *overlay* query. Fix: `grammar()` returns an owned `String` and CONCATENATES the
    base query + overlay (`format!("{}\n{}", js::HIGHLIGHT_QUERY, ts::HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY)`); the superset grammar
    resolves the base patterns. Without this, TS `const` / C++ `return` mis-classified.
  - **Per-grammar const-name variance:** most expose `HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY`, but js/c/cpp use `HIGHLIGHT_QUERY`
    (singular); `tree-sitter-typescript` ships TWO languages (`LANGUAGE_TYPESCRIPT` + `LANGUAGE_TSX`, one shared
    query). Verified each crate's exact API.
  - **`tree-sitter-kotlin-ng` ships NO highlights query** (only `LANGUAGE` + `NODE_TYPES`). Vendored a minimal
    `KOTLIN_HIGHLIGHTS` const. Trap: `true`/`false`/`null` are NAMED nodes (boolean_literal/null_literal), not
    anonymous token strings — including them as `@constant.builtin` string-literals fails the WHOLE query (one bad
    pattern poisons it); removed them. Confirmed against `node-types.json`.
- **Self-validated on host** (policy: these paths have real host coverage, unlike SwiftUI render): engine `9/0`
  (per-language token-kind assertions incl. Swift string + Kotlin keyword), TUI `mdvcore-tui` `57/0` (TestBackend
  per-cell `.fg`), web `mdvcore-web` `75/0` (HTML `<span class="tok-…">`). rust-core merge gate `^EXIT=0` with
  highlight + grammar deps confirmed ABSENT from it (scoped out of `default-members`, like ratatui). Teeth shown

- **Minimal-deps posture honoured:** all 14 new crates are owner-approved (the TSK-257 park "Approve tree-sitter +

## LOG 2026-06-08 (latest+86) — TSK-257 increment 2: TUI source view is syntax-highlighted (TestBackend fg teeth)

Wired the highlight engine into the **TUI source view** (commit `06db6b5`). Two parts:
- **Engine `highlight_lines(src, lang) -> Vec<Vec<Segment>>`** — projects the byte-range spans onto LINES (one
  `Vec<Segment>` per `\n`-split line), gaps emitted as `TokenKind::Other` so a line's segments reconstruct it
  exactly. The byte→line mapping lives here (host-testable), so front-ends stay thin. 3 new engine teeth: line
  alignment + 1-per-line count; segment-reconstruct invariant incl. a UTF-8 multibyte string (`"café ☕"`);
  empty/blank lines.
- **TUI `ViewBody::Text` arm** maps each line's segments to ratatui `Color` via a `token_color` palette
  (keyword→Magenta, string→Green, number/const→Yellow, comment→DarkGray, fn/tag→Blue, type/prop/attr→Cyan;
  structural tokens uncoloured), composed with the existing line-number gutter. **Gated** to Text mode + a
  recognised extension + NOT whitespace-reveal/flash, so HEX (shares the arm), plain text, and the reveal/flash
  overlays are untouched. **Alignment fix that matters:** the core's display lines are tab-expanded + `\r`-stripped,
  so raw-byte offsets would mis-align — the TUI feeds `lines.join("\n")` (the displayed text) to the engine.
  **Perf:** highlight computed once per file into a `RefCell` cache on `Preview` (200k-line file cap → no
  per-frame reparse).

**Teeth (TestBackend per-cell fg — the host pixel coverage the SwiftUI render path lacks):** a `.rs` fixture's
letters carry Magenta(keyword) + Green(string); a `.txt` file and HEX mode carry neither (lang gate + mode gate).
**Teeth demonstrated:** neutering `token_color` to always-None turns the highlight test red
(`{Black,Reset,DarkGray,Cyan}` — no Magenta/Green), then restored. `mdvcore-highlight` 8/0, `mdvcore-tui` 57/0;
rust-core merge gate green (highlight + tui stay scoped out of it via `default-members`).

## LOG 2026-06-08 (latest+78) — TSK-342: ImageEditorViewModel — host-testable editor model layer (image PoC UI enablement)

Rotated off test-sweeping to real product work (owner's "build PoCs: image editing" directive). The
image-editing ENGINE was already complete + host-tested (TSK-344: ImageDocument op-list + Renderer with
crop/resize/orient/colorControls/exposure/shadowHighlight/sharpen + histogram + export, 32/0) but had NO UI
wiring — the explicit "v0 spine" gap (TSK-342). Delivered the host-testable model layer any editor view
binds to (commit `46c662a`): `ImageEditorViewModel` (@MainActor ObservableObject, `Sources/ViewerUI/`).

Design that earns real host teeth despite the UI being render-gated:
- Live tonal sliders are STATE (brightness/contrast/saturation/exposure/shadow/highlight/sharpness), folded
  into ONE op each at render time via the `document` computed property — a slider drag mutates a single
  derived op, never spamming the lossless history. Identity sliders contribute nothing (pristine = source).
- Geometry ops (crop/resize/orient) commit to the lossless history with `undoGeometry()`.
- Republishes the rendered preview `CGImage` + `Histogram`; renders headless via Core Image (no window).
- Made `Renderer.histogram` public (the editor needs it, like the already-public `render`).

Host teeth (7 tests, ImageEditorViewModelTests, all green): pristine init; brightness lightens the pixel AND
folds to exactly one colorControls op (re-drag does NOT append — the no-spam guard); saturation 0 greys out
(R≈G≈B); geometry resize halves dims + undo restores; resetTonal returns the pixel to pristine while keeping
geometry; revertAll clears both; identity sliders add no ops. These exercise the real slider→op→pixel path
through the tested engine — a regression (op-spam, wrong direction, broken undo) trips them.

TSK-342 stays at `fixed`: the SwiftUI editor view that draws the preview + sliders + histogram is the
render-gated remainder (VM/human gate via the now-unblocked TSK-502 pixel lane). NEXT image increment: that
thin view + a VM pixel/AX test.

## LOG 2026-06-08 (latest+76) — TSK-519: VisualRegression ModeBar false-positive fixed (Retina scale heuristic) — stale-test sweep #2

The T5 pixel VisualRegression sweep (second use of the TSK-502-unblocked lane) flagged
`SourceViewVisualRegressionTests.test_allUIStripsCompositeAfterOpeningSourceFile`: "Region 'ModeBar'
appears uniform — the SwiftUI sibling-blank compositor regression has likely returned." Given CLAUDE.md's
4×-recurrence warning on that exact class, I treated it as possibly-real and went to the pixels: pulled the
surviving `.fail.png` (2200×1600) off the VM and viewed it — **the app composites perfectly** (tab bar,
Editor/HEX/View-Only ModeBar, sidebar, syntax-highlighted source, terminal, status bar all present). NOT a
regression.

Root cause (PIL-confirmed on the screenshot): `scaleY = max(1, Int(h/900))` returns **1** for the VM's
1600px-tall **2×** capture, so all three sample bands collapse into the top ~92px of window chrome; the
ModeBar band (y60..92) lands on a flat title-bar strip → 1 distinct colour → false "uniform". TabBar and
StatusBar passed by luck (title text / bottom edge). Same class as TSK-517 (geometry drift while the lane
was TCC-blocked).

Fix (commit `4c033d6`, test-only): `capturedBackingScale()` derives the true device-px-per-point from the
window's `CGWindowBounds` (points) vs the captured pixel width — correct on 1×/2× alike — replacing both
`Int(h/900)` sites; widened the ModeBar band 32→48pt so it reaches the content rows (robust 13-colour
margin vs the marginal 3). VM-validated on the disclaim lane: BOTH tests pass — main (healthy) 8.314s +
meta-teeth (broken-ruler) 5.385s. **Teeth:** the buggy scale made the main test RED (the very sweep that
surfaced this); the meta-teeth test was previously passing TRIVIALLY (always-uniform ModeBar) and now
detects the injected blank for the right reason. TSK-519 reported→…→fixed; validating on host-gate green.

## LOG 2026-06-08 (latest+69) — TSK-516: rust-core indent CRLF A/B-parity bug — found + fixed + VALIDATED

A genuinely-new rust-core bug found by chasing a lead (NOT another already-fixed audit finding).
Probing board TSK-276 confirmed the numbering trap again (board TSK-276 = "[BACKLOG] Debugger", not
the IndentDetector finding — already flagged for owner), but it pointed at a real question: the SWIFT
IndentDetector handles CRLF (fixed long ago) — does the RUST port? It did NOT.

`mdvcore-core::indent::detect` splits on `'\n'` but kept the trailing `'\r'`, so a whitespace-only
CRLF line `"  \r"` failed the all-whitespace skip (CR isn't space/tab) and was miscounted as a
2-space indent. Concrete A/B divergence from the shipping Swift detector: `detect("\tfoo\n  \r\n",50)`
→ Rust `"Mixed"` vs Swift `"Tabs"`; a 4-space CRLF file with blank `"  \r"` lines mis-detected as
`"Spaces (2)"` (spurious width-2 lines outscore width-4 since 2 divides 4). **Root cause it slipped:
the `IndentDetectABTests` A/B corpus had ZERO CRLF cases.**

Fix (commit `15af4eb`): one-line `strip_suffix('\r')` per line + 3 Rust unit teeth + 4 CRLF cases
added to the A/B corpus. Filed as **TSK-516** (new), walked reported→…→**validated** (agent
self-validate — pure-logic rust-core + FFI A/B is host-testable, no VM). Teeth DEMONSTRATED red→green:
reverted the strip → 2 of 3 Rust tests went red (`"Mixed"`, `"Spaces (2)"`) → restored → green.
rust-core gate green; FFI `.a` rebuilt; Swift A/B parity green.

LESSON: the "deep-audit findings are mostly-already-fixed" pattern holds for the SWIFT side, but a
fixed-in-Swift finding can still be LIVE in the Rust port — check both sides of an A/B pair. And an
A/B parity test only guards what its corpus covers (the CRLF gap here).

## LOG 2026-06-08 (latest+59) — TSK-485 VALIDATED: LSPPool.closeAll() parallelized + deterministic teeth

SwiftUI/ViewerCore tick (SwiftUI lane first per SOP). Picked up the executable spec I left
on TSK-485 last tick and shipped it. Commit `6703798`, board TSK-485 → **validated**.

The leak: `LSPPool.closeAll()` shut live clients down SEQUENTIALLY; each `LSPClient.shutdown()`
costs up to ~2.4s, so with N≥2 live servers (sourcekit-lsp + a TS server, say) teardown was
N×2.4s and blew past the bounded app-quit deadline — un-shut servers got reparented to launchd.

Three-part fix, all in `6703798`:
- **`LSPPool.closeAll()`** — sequential `for` → `await withTaskGroup(of: Key.self)`: children call
  `client.shutdown()` and return their `Sendable` `Key`; the actor-isolated parent is the sole
  mutator of `entries`. Outer drain-while loop preserved (catches a late `.live` spawn past the
  `isClosed` latch). Teardown is now ≈ slowest single shutdown, not the sum.
- **app-quit** (`MarkdownViewer/main.swift`) — the 15s budget was already widened in a prior
  in-file patch; with parallel closeAll it's now a pure safety ceiling (8s) and **logs a warning
  on timeout** instead of silently leaking (the finding's explicit ask). The stale "can't
  parallelize from here" comment updated.
- **test teardown** — 4 LSP smoke tests' fire-and-forget `defer { Task { await …closeAll()/shutdown() } }`
  → awaited `self.addTeardownBlock { … }` so child LSP processes are reaped synchronously between
  tests (the second merged finding — leaked children during test runs).

Deterministic teeth (no flaky wall-clock, despite the known-flaky LSP subsystem cf TSK-507):
added `MDV_FAKE_LSP_SHUTDOWN_DELAY_MS` + `MDV_FAKE_LSP_SHUTDOWN_LOG` knobs to `MDVFakeLSPServer`
(shutdown handler brackets the delay with `START`/`END` markers via one atomic `O_APPEND` write;
`LSPClient.shutdown()` awaits the shutdown response, so the delay lands on the awaited path). New
test: 3 live servers @ 400ms delay, assert all 3 STARTs precede the first END — pure ORDERING.
**Teeth proven:** reverted closeAll to sequential → test FAILED red (`lastStart 4 !< firstEnd 1`,
markers `[START,END,START,END,START,END]`, 8.04s vs 0.65s parallel), then restored.

Validation: LSPPoolFakeServerTests 18 passed; LSP smoke tests pass (real sourcekit reaped
synchronously); `bash scripts/test-headless-gate.sh` → headless gate PASSED + tier enforcement OK
(4311 tests). Self-validated (actor behavior, host-testable, teeth-proven). Honest scope note on
the validation: the app-quit timeout *warning-log* branch is app-code with no host coverage for
the timeout path itself, but it's a trivial log on an already-bounded wait and the leak it guards
is eliminated at the source by the test-proven concurrency.

## LOG 2026-06-07 (latest+58) — self-review found + fixed a real crash in my own JSON formatter

Autonomous tick. Instead of grabbing another PORT feature, reviewed THIS session's
rust-core additions for problems before they spread — and found one. Commit `f47c7d3`.

- **Bug:** `format::pretty_json` (shipped this session for TSK-217/218, already validated)
  is recursive with NO depth bound. A balanced deeply-nested `.json` (`[[[[…]]]]`) overflows
  the stack → `panic=abort` → whole-process crash. Shared core ⇒ reachable from every
  front-end opening an untrusted file. Same class as the cmark deep-nesting SIGSEGV (TSK-126).
- **Fix:** `MAX_DEPTH = 128` cap in `value()` (matches serde_json) → returns None past it →
  raw-text fallback, no crash. Test `deeply_nested_input_is_bounded_not_overflowed` on
  balanced 100k-deep input. **Teeth-proven:** neutering the cap aborts the test with SIGABRT;
  restored → clean None. rust-core gate green.
- Logged the durable lesson (LESSONS.md → "Recursive-descent parsers need a depth cap") +
  commented the hardening on TSK-217. Reinforces: validated ≠ unimpeachable; a self-review
  pass on freshly-shipped core code is worth a tick.

  hex-byte pattern first (`"41"`, `"ff 7f"`, `"deadbeef"`) via

- **New field** `App.find_is_hex` gates the mode-force skip + the label; reset in
  `clear_find` and on every no-match. `HEX_BYTES_PER_ROW = 16` const documents
  the row math (must track `hex::render_all`).

  whole path via the in-memory `App` + `render()` snapshot (no real terminal):
  `data.bin` (`00 41 ff 7f`) → `/41` → 1 match on row 0, view stays `Hex`,
  status renders `hex: 1 of 1`; then `/0000` → empty matches + hex-labelled
  model status. Has teeth: fails on wrong row math, mode-force, or missing label.
- **Honesty note:** the no-match status lives in `App.status` (the bottom bar
  falls back to browse help on a miss — same as the text find), so that
  assertion checks the model field, not `render()`. `cargo test -p mdvcore-tui
  hex` → 4 pass; `scripts/rust-core-gate.sh` green.

## LOG 2026-06-07 (latest+48) — TSK-488 REAL FIX: terminal tabs were compositor-occluded (validated w/ real pixels)

The recurring "I see a gap before the terminal but no tabs" — finally root-caused and fixed with REAL
compositor-pixel proof, not another symptom guess. Commits `1dd0483` (fix) + `a99e978` (test);
TSK-488 → **validated** (self, with a teeth-proven T5 test).

- **Root cause = compositor occlusion.** The opaque, layer-backed `TerminalNSView`
  (`NSViewRepresentable`) overdrew its sibling SwiftUI tab strip when the strip was drawn BEFORE it in
  the stack (`.left`/`.top`). Drawn AFTER (`.right`) it was fine — which is exactly why the owner, on the
  default LEFT, saw nothing. The prior four "fixes" (ScrollView removal, accent colour, widen rail) were
  all chasing symptoms.
- **Fix:** force each strip into its own compositing layer ordered above the surface —
  `strip.compositingGroup().zIndex(1)` vs `terminalSurface.zIndex(0)` in all three position cases
  (`TerminalView.swift`). Verified with `screencapture -l<windowID>` for left/top/right; I visually
  inspected the rail crops — terminal glyph + "1" chip + accent-blue selected chip + "+" + close all
  paint in the rail.
- **The owner's "test is broken" was right.** The headless `ImageRenderer` test was a FALSE GREEN — it
  rasterizes SwiftUI's own drawing in isolation, never instantiates the opaque AppKit layer, so it
  passed while the live window was blank. Replaced it: renamed to `TerminalTabStripRasterTests` (honest
  scope: chip colour/layout only) + added `TerminalTabStripVisualRegressionTests` (T5 `PixelTestCase`)
  that captures the REAL window via `MDV_UI_SCENE` + `screencapture`. **Proven to have teeth:** reverted
  the fix, rebuilt, ran it → FAILS for left+top (passes for right, correctly). Restored + reinstalled.
- Headless gate green (4150); fixed debug bundle installed to `/Applications`. Lessons captured in
  `LESSONS.md` (opaque-representable occlusion + ImageRenderer false-green + "always demonstrate teeth").

## LOG 2026-06-07 (latest+39) — REAL security bug found + fixed: ReDoS guard group-prefix (TSK-293/279)

First genuinely-unfixed board item this session. The ReDoS shape guard
(`RegexComplexityGuard`) skipped a group's `(?…` modifier prefix by consuming any run of
`[A-Za-z:=!<]` — which over-consumed and let catastrophic patterns slip past `reject()`:
- `(?<name>a+)+` — `>` not consumed → became the group's first atom, defeating the
  `firstAtomQuantified` check (TSK-293, named groups).
- `(?:a+)+` — after `:` it kept eating letters → body atom `a` swallowed, inner `+` quantified
  nothing (TSK-279 — a real hole, not just a missing test).
- `(?:a|aa)+` / `(?<g>a|aa)+` — same corruption defeated the alternation-overlap check.
All are exponential ReDoS that the find/MCP-find/cross-file-search paths must reject. **Fix
(`c7a9bb8`):** replaced the loose inline skip in BOTH heuristics with a precise shared
`skipGroupPrefix()` (handles `(?:`,`(?=`,`(?!`,`(?<=`,`(?<!`,`(?<name>`,`(?P<name>`,`(?flags:`/`(?flags)`).
10 tests: 6 newly-caught ReDoS forms + 4 benign forms that must still pass (anchored `(?:\.\d+)+`,
named bounded body, inline flags, look-around). Headless gate green (FoldBench load-flake only).
Note: this is a host-validatable real bug — disproves "queue fully drained"; the audit list still
holds the occasional genuine miss, so verify-first remains worthwhile (just not blind closing).

## LOG 2026-06-06 (latest+31) — owner two-bug batch: terminal latency + 2nd prod-app-nuke site

Owner reported two bugs interactively; both fixed, gated, committed, and the fresh debug
bundle installed to `/Applications/TextView.app` (owner must relaunch to pick up new code).

- **BUG #2 — "headless test STILL nuking /Applications/TextView" (`f6499fe`):** a SECOND
  by-exec-name kill site after the `install-app.sh` killall (`e5ffa08`). `LaunchHarness.cleanup()`
  did `AppLauncher.currentPID(of: "MarkdownViewer").map { kill($0, SIGTERM) }` — `currentPID` is a
  raw `pgrep -x`-by-name lookup, so it SIGTERM'd the owner's running prod app (shared exec name).
  Fires in heavy-tier TEAR-DOWN, which runs **even when the body self-skips in the gate** (setUp/
  tearDown still execute around a skipped test) — so the window-free gate WAS killing the app.
  Fixed: route through `AppLauncher.killTestInstances(named:)` (MDV_TEST_INSTANCE-scoped). Lesson:
  the footgun isn't only `killall`, and "self-skip" doesn't cover tear-down. (LESSONS + memory
  `feedback-killall-footgun` updated.)
- **BUG #1 — "terminal very slow typing/Enter" (`d8141c5`):** root cause = `TerminalModel.scheduleBump`
  was a PURELY TRAILING-edge throttle — every keystroke echo spawned a Task that slept a full frame
  (≥16ms, more under Task.sleep imprecision) BEFORE bumping `version`, so input never painted until a
  frame after the shell echoed, even on an idle prompt. Replaced with a LEADING-edge throttle (new
  pure `ViewerCore/Terminal/FrameThrottle.swift`, headlessly tested): first event after idle paints
  immediately, then 16ms cooldown coalesces the burst + one trailing flush. Also memoized the 256
  ansi/indexed `NSColor` palette (was allocating per attribute-run per frame — 256/truecolor churn in
  the draw path). New tests: `FrameThrottleTests` (ViewerCore), `TerminalPaletteTests` (ViewerUI,
  memoization + value-equivalence). Headless gate GREEN (4067 tests, tier enforcement OK).
- **Board down:** `localhost:8787` unreachable this turn — couldn't advance board tasks to `fixed`.
  Recorded here; create/advance TSK entries for both fixes when the board is back up.

## LOG 2026-06-06 (latest+23) — ROOT-CAUSE FIX: session-index clobber guard (TSK-438 fixed)
- Continued from the session-tab diagnosis. Shipped the durable fix the owner actually wants (the Reset
  menu was only the escape hatch).
- **TSK-438 FIXED (`bf395f9`):** `SessionStore` now refuses to persist an EMPTY `SessionIndex` while
  `liveSnapshotIDs()` (non-trashed `<uuid>.json` files) is non-empty — at BOTH write entry points
  (`saveIndexSync`, `enqueueSaveIndex`). Keeps the prior index + logs to stderr. That is the exact
  clobber signature (empty index.json next to live snapshots → empty strip). A legitimate close-all has
  already trashed its snapshot, so `liveSnapshotIDs()` is empty and the empty write proceeds. Store-level
  = one chokepoint, robust regardless of which coordinator race (#330) triggers it.
- **Validation:** 5 ViewerCore unit tests (`SessionIndexClobberGuardTests`) + `swift build` +
  `scripts/test-headless-gate.sh` = **exit 0, PASSED** on the committed commit (no session-test
  regressions; this run was fully clean — perf benches passed too).
- **FOLLOW-UP (optional, not blocking):** auto-rebuild the index from orphaned snapshots on restore
  (selective — ~40 stale tiny test snapshots on the owner machine). The Reset menu + this guard already
  cover recover + prevent-recurrence, so this is a nice-to-have.
- `main` @ guard commit, single linear trunk, headless-gate-green.

- Owner asked for bigger 20–30min tasks (keep the session busy). Took the line-hover-highlight cross-view

  caret/selection current-line highlight.
  - **Source view (NSTextView):** new `SourceHoverHighlight` SwiftUI overlay drawn as a *non-interactive*
    sibling in a `ZStack`; `.onContinuousHover` on the container maps pointer→line via
    `SourceHoverGeometry` (the exact inverse of `SourceGutterView`'s coordinate math), painting a
    theme-aware backdrop, suppressed on the caret line + clipped to the viewport.
  - **Design choice (why this over alternatives):** the current-line + find highlights use NSLayoutManager
    temporary `.backgroundColor` attributes → a hover via the same mechanism would *collide* (wiped on
    caret move / find update). A `drawBackground` subclass would mean rebuilding the delicate
    `scrollableTextView()` setup (non-contiguous layout, gutter reentrancy). The SwiftUI-overlay path
    (mirroring the existing gutter sibling) is conflict-free, doesn't intercept clicks/selection, and
    needs zero NSTextView changes.
  - **Editor (CM6):** theme-aware `.cm-line:hover` CSS rule (`body.dark`/`body.light`).
- **Validation:** pure pointer→line kernel unit-tested headlessly (`SourceHoverGeometryTests`, 6 cases:
  scroll offset, top-inset, past-last-line boundary, degenerate geometry, viewport-y round-trip) — found
  + fixed my own off-by-a-row test-boundary bug (kernel was correct). Headless gate green (tier-clean) +
  live T4 ViewModeMatrix 3/3. The hover *interaction* is mouse-driven (not gate-exercisable) → human
  review is the visual confirm.

## LOG 2026-06-06 (latest+14) — 🚀 PERF FIX#1 LANDED (TSK-108 → fixed): per-tab pane retention, instant tab switch
- **This is the loudest real pain killed** — the perf cluster's dominant view-side fix, NOT a paper cut.
  Switching tabs tore down + reloaded the WKWebView-backed panes (rendered-markdown / CM6 editor) ~1s;
  A→B→A reloaded twice. Root cause was view-side (model already minimal: 1 republish/switch).
- **Implementation (commit `39925fd`, landed on main via ff):** `ContentView.content` now renders a
  `ZStack` of ALL **mounted** tab panes (the `MountedPanesLRU`, cap 4, held `@Published` on
  `DocumentModel`), not just the active one. Inactive panes stay mounted (gated `opacity:0` /
  `allowsHitTesting(false)` / `accessibilityHidden`) → switch-back is a pure visibility flip, **zero
  WKWebView teardown+reload**. `dismantleNSView` fires only on LRU tail eviction.
  - Single driver: the LRU is reconciled entirely from the universal `updateDerived()` hook
    (`retainOnly(open)` + `activate(selected)`), change-guarded so a non-selection republish adds no
    `objectWillChange`. No per-callsite wiring in selectTab/closeTab/session-switch.
  - `tabContent(for:isActive:)` reads each pane's OWN `state`/`viewMode`/`id` (not the active tab's);
    find bar + find query gated on `isActive` so only the visible pane shows/drives find (no
    first-responder fight). `opacity:0` (not `.hidden()`) avoids WebKit `visibilitychange`→self-reload
    (cmux #1228).
- **Validation (all green, no owner staring):**
  1. Headless merge gate — `scripts/test-headless-gate.sh`: **3975 tests pass, tier-clean**.
  2. NEW `MountedPanesWiringTests` (bare gate, WKWebView-free retention-set teeth) — **mutation-checked**
     (broke retention → test fails → restored).
  3. NEW `PaneRetentionMountProbeTests` (`MDV_RUN_WEBVIEW_TESTS` lane) — on the REAL view tree:
     **A→B→A = 0 WKWebView makes/dismantles**; LRU overflow = exactly **1** dismantle. (DEBUG-only
     `MountProbe` counters in both representables.)
  4. Live T4 `ViewModeMatrixSmokeTests` on the assembled `dist/TextView.app` (`scripts/build-app.sh
     debug`) — **3/3 green**: every (file type × view mode) renders correctly, lazy-materialize intact.
- **Board:** TSK-108 → `fixed` (agent terminal lane). Remaining is the human `review→validated→done`
  supervised visual/interaction pass (the *feel* of instant switch, no flicker on heavy docs) — that's
  the only thing the automated gates can't assert. Branch reaped; main single-threaded + gate-green.

## LOG 2026-06-06 (latest+12) — HEX-perf spike (TSK-267 → triaged); headless lanes exhausted
- **Perf-debug spike on the HEX slowness** (TSK-267 "1MB extreme" / #218 "6KB ~1s"). Ruled out the
  model layer: `HexDumpBuilder.renderRows` is algorithmically clean (raw-pointer `withUnsafeBytes`,
  `reserveCapacity`, amortized-O(1) appends) — a 6KB dump builds in µs, 1MB in <100 ms. The cost is
  view-layer: `HexView` builds the **entire** dump as **one** `NSAttributedString` (no windowing) → TextKit
  lays out a multi-MB monospaced grid in one shot (the 1MB killer); the 6KB ~1s is too small to be dump
  size → fixed per-open overhead (mode-switch remount / async load / layout). Fix = virtualized NSTextView
  rendering + avoid full remount on mode switch — **view-layer, no headless fix** (matches TSK-267's own
  report). Board TSK-267 → `triaged`, flagged `live-validation`, model layer ruled out for the live turn.
- **STATE: the headless lanes are now exhausted.** Across this owner-away run (13 firings) I've drained:
  feature cores that don't need live (Tools surface), command-wiring/Omni (7 commands, TSK-411–414),
  pure-logic test backfill (+67 tests, TSK-415–419), and now the perf spikes — every remaining

  manufacture headless work would mean low-value tests for covered code or risky blind view edits —

## LOG 2026-06-06 (latest+2) — Save a Copy engine LANDED (TSK-300, headless), menu deferred
- Challenged the "pool drained" conclusion: there IS a headless-shippable SwiftUI class — **@MainActor
  model/command logic** drivable via ScriptVerb/HeadlessHarness (not pixel rendering). TSK-300 fits.
- **`6c2fc9e` feat(save): Save a Copy engine + `save-copy` verb.** `DocumentModel.saveCopy(ofTabAt:to:)`
  + `saveCopyOfCurrentTab(to:)` write the tab's CURRENT effective content to a NEW path, leaving the
  open tab untouched (no save, no retarget, no dirty-flag change). Content precedence: HEX-dirty bytes
  → dirty editor text (buffer encoding) → verbatim on-disk file. Production-grade write: atomic for the
  dirty cases, temp-then-`replaceItemAt` for overwrite (no data-loss window), `copyItem` streaming for
  clean files (no memory slurp, attribute-preserving). Exposed as the `save-copy <path>` ScriptVerb —
  **automation/MCP-reachable today**. 9 headless tests (3 content sources + tab-unchanged invariant +
  overwrite + noTab/emptyTab/no-selection). Headless gate green (3791 tests).
- Board: **TSK-300 → `progress`**, flagged `live-validation`. **Remaining (live turn):** the thin
  user-facing wire-up `File > Save a Copy…` → `NSSavePanel` → `saveCopyOfCurrentTab(to:)` (needs a
  window to validate). The risky/correctness-heavy core is done + tested; the live part is ~10 min.
- Pattern confirmed for the owner-away headless lane: ship the tested model/command CORE + a script

## LOG 2026-06-06 — adversarial self-audit of TSK-410 found + fixed a silent Rust regression
- **`ef05840` fix(highlight): repair rust @constant query typo** (TSK-410 follow-up). Audited every
  grammar query's `#match?` regex for NSRegularExpression mis-evaluation now that predicates are
  honored (TSK-410). Found ONE latent typo it activated: `rust-highlights.scm` matched
  SCREAMING_CASE with `^[A-Z][A-Z\d_]+$'` — the stray trailing quote = end-anchor + literal quote,
  which never matches. Harmless while predicates were ignored; once evaluated, Rust constants
  silently lost `.constant` coloring (no golden covered it). Dropped the quote + added `testRust`
  (MAX_SIZE → .constant). Other 13 grammars' `#match` regexes verified NSRegularExpression-safe;
  a rescan for `$<char>` never-match patterns found no others. Gate green (3764).
  **Lesson:** enabling query-predicate evaluation can activate latent broken-regex typos that were
  dead while predicates were ignored — audit all `#match` patterns when flipping that on.
- Also extended TSK-410 regression coverage to JavaScript (`2cc59e9`, prior heartbeat).

## LOG 2026-06-05 (latest) — TSK-410 predicate evaluation FIXED
- **`5e840b3` fix(highlight): evaluate tree-sitter query predicates** (TSK-410 → `fixed`).
  `TreeSitterEngine.tokenize` now routes the query cursor through SwiftTreeSitter's
  `resolve(with: Predicate.Context)` so `#match?`/`#eq?`/`#any-of?` are evaluated. The
  textProvider returns each node's source slice; the default group-membership provider keeps
  `#is-not? local` satisfied → **no currently-rendered capture is dropped**, only wrongly-firing
  regex/eq captures are filtered. `const myThing = 5` → `myThing` is now `.variable` (was `.type`).
  Fixes broad TS/JS identifier mis-coloring in the Source view + markdown code fences.
- Caught a dependent test: the cpp smoke snippet (`std::vector<int> v;`) only ever produced a run
  via the bug (`std` lowercase namespace_identifier wrongly matched `#match? "^[A-Z]"`). Restated
  to `class C { auto x = nullptr; };` (real captures). Golden `testPredicatesAreEvaluated` added.
  Headless gate green (3762). **Lesson:** a smoke that only asserts "produces runs" can silently
  depend on buggy output — see LESSONS.
- **Bonus:** predicate eval now UNBLOCKS JSX `@tag`/`@attribute` coloring for `.tsx` (the bogus
  `@type` is filtered for lowercase tags) — a small follow-up could re-add a tsx-highlights query.

  CI, headless + rust gates: all unaffected/green; the `.highlight` gate ships OFF so behavior
  is unchanged. Options: (1) transient bump to ~64/44, reclaim at stage 4 (Swift grammar
  deletion) — end state ~55/40 since grammars move from dlopen'd Frameworks/ dylibs INTO the
  exec; (2) ship rust highlight as a dlopen'd dylib like the Swift lazy grammars — exec cap
  intact, extra plumbing; (3) cargo-feature grammars OFF in the app's staticlib (remote-only
  highlight) until remote is primary. **My recommendation: (2) if the 26 MB exec cap is a hard
  principle, else (1).** Stage 3 (+10 grammar crates for 22-language parity) waits on this too.

  would diverge. **Options:** (a) approve `unicode-segmentation` (~1 small, widely
  used crate) for a fully-faithful port; (b) ship a scalar-domain port with a
  documented "ASCII/BMP-single-scalar only" limitation + a gate-OFF default; (c)
  leave FuzzyMatcher in Swift (it's cheap; the migration value is "one core" reuse,
  not speed). **My default if unanswered: (c) leave in Swift** — lowest risk, no
  dep, and fuzzy scoring is not a hot path. Deferred, not blocking.

  existing line-jump machinery** — the current match's line becomes the goto `target`, getting the same
  `id="L<n>"` anchor + `.cur` highlight go-to-line already uses — so there's ZERO mid-line HTML-escaping
  surgery (correct by construction). Minimal-churn threading (`render_view` stays a thin wrapper; only
  `render_view_filtered`/`content_html` gained the 2 params). **Validated on the committed commit:**

  - `HexCaretMap` / `HexLayout` caret↔offset mapping and
    `HexSearchEngine.offsets(ofByte:)` are **tiny pure arithmetic** (`offset /
    width`, single-byte scan). The FFI marshalling cost exceeds any benefit and
    a TUI/web front-end would trivially reimplement them — porting these would be
    manufacturing marginal work (which this doc explicitly warns against). Left
    in Swift by design, not by omission.
  - **#6 FuzzyMatcher** — its `matchedIndices` are **grapheme** (Swift
    `Character`) indices; Rust `str` iterates **scalars**. Byte-exact parity on
    combining-mark / ZWJ-emoji targets needs a grapheme-segmentation crate
    (`unicode-segmentation`, owner-gated). A scalar-domain port would silently
    diverge there — incompatible with the honest byte-for-byte A/B discipline
    every shipped slice has held. Deferred to an owner dep decision.
  - **#8 FileIconClassifier** — output is ViewerKit's `FileIconKind` (enum with
    associated values); RustCore can't import ViewerKit, so a port needs a
    parallel Rust enum + Swift remap, **doubling** a 290-line drift-prone mapping
    table, for "low value." Not worth the maintenance surface vs the payoff.
