### KEY FINDINGS (this headless wave, 2026-06-04 morning)
- **Tab-op republish is NOT the bottleneck.** RepublishCountTests measured: warm
  same-mode `selectTab` fires EXACTLY 1 `DocumentModel.objectWillChange`
  (mean=1.0, worst=1); `closeTab` worst=2. The model side is already minimal →
  the live tab freeze is **entirely view-side** (cost of reacting to that 1
  republish: full ContentView re-eval + WebView reload). **Implication for the
  live perf turn:** Fix#1 (per-tab view RETENTION) is the only lever that
  matters; Fix#2/#3 (model-side republish trimming) are marginal (1→0). Don't
  spend the live turn on them. Guard bounds (switch≤4/close≤6) catch a fan-out
  regression now; tighten to 0 only after Fix#2 ships.
- **#218 (HEX 6KB ~1s) is view-side, not model-side.** HexDumpBuilder is a clean
  single-pass build; a 6KB file is ONE chunk (defaultRowsPerChunk=4096). The
  existing `test_microbench_4MB_firstChunk_isFast` already proves even a 4MB
  first-chunk build is <500ms. So #218's ~1s is the mode-switch view remount /
  Task.detached→main.sync scheduling vs a busy main thread — SAME cluster as
  #219. Fold #218 into the live perf turn; no headless fix exists.

## LOG +83 (2026-06-08, autonomous tick — core XML/HTML pretty-print)
- **Shipped TSK-496 [PORT] XML/HTML pretty-print** (commit ddecc1d), validated.
  The deferred half of the Formatted-mode slice (JSON landed in TSK-217); this
  completes XML parity with the SwiftUI FormatViewer.
- **Impl (all in `crates/core`, no new dep):** `format::pretty_xml(&str)->
  Option<String>` — a hand-rolled tokenizer (`Tok::Open/Close/Leaf/Other/Text`)
  → depth-balancer → iterative emitter reusing the existing 2-space `INDENT`.
  Rules: xml-decl / comments / CDATA / DOCTYPE kept **verbatim**; tag-end scan is
  quote-aware so `>` inside an attribute value doesn't end the tag; DOCTYPE scan
  is bracket+quote-aware; a single text-or-other child is **inlined**
  (`<b>hi</b>`, `<d><![CDATA[..]]></d>`); self-closing tags don't open a level;
  unbalanced/malformed input → `None` (caller falls back to raw text). All using
  `.get()`/no-indexing per the core crate's no-panic clippy denies.
- **Wiring:** `view::classify` now maps `.xml/.svg/.plist/.xib/.storyboard` →
  `FileKind::Structured` (so Formatted is offered); `formatted_lines` does
  `pretty_json.or_else(pretty_xml)`. No front-end changes — `ViewMode::Formatted`
  is already generic in TUI/web. This also un-deadens the `.svg` formatted-mode
  path flagged by deep-audit TSK-307.
- **Teeth:** 9 `format::tests::xml_*` cases (nesting+inline-leaf, attrs+self-close,
  `>`-in-attr, decl/comment/CDATA verbatim, empty-inline, per-level indent, svg,
  idempotent, malformed→None) + `view::tests::formatted_mode_reindents_xml_via_
  shared_core` (build `doc.xml` Formatted → the reflow, not raw) + classify
  assertions. Each asserts exact output so any reflow regression fails. core 253
  passed/0 failed; rust-core gate exit 0; `cargo build --workspace` green.
- **Gate fix during this tick:** initial test used `let ... else { panic!() }`,
  which the core `clippy::panic` deny rejected (cargo test alone passed — the
  gate's stricter lints caught it). Switched to the `match { .. _ => unreachable!() }`
  pattern the existing view tests use (`unreachable!` isn't flagged by
  `clippy::panic`).

- Third model-first SwiftUI slice this run. **TSK-310** "[BACKLOG] A filter button on
  Files pane … fuzzy [narrow the tree]" → **progress** (commit `654015b`). Board id
  verified (`task_get` TSK-310 = the Files-pane filter task).
- **Slice 1 (CORE, done + host-validated):** new `Sources/ViewerCore/FileTreeFilter.swift`
  — pure enum, generic over the caller's node via closures (id/children/isMatch), so
  matching stays decoupled (the existing `FuzzyMatcher` plugs in as `isMatch`). The
  genuinely-missing piece was the narrowing RULE, not the matcher:
  `visibleIDs(...) -> Set<ID>` keeps a node if it matches, OR an ancestor matches (a
  matched folder reveals its whole subtree), OR a descendant matches (the path down to
  each match stays); only real self/descendant matches propagate upward so siblings of a
  matched folder aren't retained. Teeth: `FileTreeFilterTests` 7/7 — leaf match keeps
  leaf+ancestors only, folder match keeps whole subtree, extension match across branches,
  root match keeps its subtree, no-match empty, empty-roots, explicit match-all. (Caught a
  Swift gotcha: `"x".contains("")` is FALSE — empty needle is NOT match-all; callers treat

## LOG +107 (2026-06-08, autonomous tick — TSK-499 slice 2b: TUI CSV cell-find wired + host-tested → TSK-499 DONE/validated)
- Closed out TSK-499 on the host-completable PORT lane: wired the shared `find::find_in_table` into
  the ratatui TUI table view (commit `4315a94`) → **TSK-499 validated** (all 3 tiers — core `37fc03d`,
  web `7f43701`, TUI `4315a94` — each regression-guarded by automated tests).
- **Design decision (UX trigger):** in table mode `/` is already the row FILTER (established, tested),
  so cell-FIND gets NO new keybinding — it's reachable via the command **palette** ("find in file" →
  `Cmd::Find` → `open_find`), which is discoverable and leaves `/` alone. Find LOCATES (highlight +
  jump), filter NARROWS; they compose (find runs over the SHOWN/filtered rows).
- **Behaviour:** `commit_find` is now table-aware (computes cell hits over shown rows; does NOT fall
  through to the text branch that would force Text mode via `jump_to_current_match`). Render highlights
  every matching cell (yellow) and marks the current `find_sel`-th hit distinctly (magenta); `n`/`N`
  step cells (`find_step` recomputes hits so stepping stays aligned after a re-filter, wraps);
  `scroll_table_to_current_hit` keeps the current hit visible without jumping a fully-visible table;
  `draw_status` shows "find: i of n cells"; ESC clears. Also made `find_in_table` GENERIC over the row
  type (`R: AsRef<[String]>`) so the TUI passes its borrowed `Vec<&Vec<String>>` slice without cloning
  (web/core still pass owned rows); fixed the core empty-table test's now-ambiguous `&[]` → typed slice.
- **Teeth (pixel-style, host):** `table_cell_find_highlights_current_steps_and_clears` drives the REAL
  palette trigger then asserts per-cell **bg** on the rendered `TestBackend` buffer (current=Magenta,
  other hit=Yellow, non-match=Reset) across commit → n-step → wrap → ESC-clear. Unlike SwiftUI CA
  layers, the ratatui render path is a deterministic in-process buffer, so this is genuine host
  coverage of the rendered behaviour (not layout-only). **Teeth DEMONSTRATED:** making the current-cell
  style non-distinct turned it red (`left: Some(Yellow), right: Some(Magenta)`), then restored → green.
- Gates: TUI suite 50/50; web 61/61; `cargo clippy -p mdvcore-tui` no NEW warnings (4→3 after factoring
  out a `type_complexity`; remaining 3 are pre-existing module-doc lints); **rust-core-gate green**
  (core 262 tests + ffi no_panic + doctests; covers the generic `find_in_table` change). main @ `4315a94`,
  tree clean. **PORT lane note:** the [PORT][TUI/WEB] W1 backlog (TSK-362..423) remains the standing

## LOG +113 (2026-06-08, autonomous tick — TSK-500 root-caused to fd-exhaustion + fixed; validation re-run in flight)
- Worked TSK-500 (the VM-lane unusability that's been blocking autonomous UI validation). CORRECTED last
  tick's wrong guess: the ~158 VM failures are NOT "ssh has no temp dir" (disproven — a fresh ssh session
  writes NSTemporaryDirectory() fine, mktemp works). REAL root cause = **file-descriptor exhaustion**:
  VM soft `ulimit -n`=256 (hard=unlimited); the full suite runs as ONE `swift test` process over ~4220
  tests; leaky fd sites (FileWatcher sources, LSP/PTY/plugin pipes) accumulate until >256 → EMFILE →
  "could not open temp file" cascade. PROOF: XattrIOTests SKIPS in the full run but PASSES 5/5 in
  isolation on the VM; TextFileLoaderTests 21/21 green on host AND on VM in isolation; `ulimit -n 8192`
  succeeds on the VM.

  before any `swift test`, with a logged limit line. Syntax-checked (`bash -n`). Synced to the VM.
- **Validation re-run in flight** (background job b0ow56msa: `test-in-vm.sh test`, capturing the limit
  line + suite summary + any residual "could not open temp"). Expect the ~158 file-IO failures to
  collapse; any residue should be only the heavy UI tiers (occlusion — they need a GUI login session,
  the remaining half of TSK-500). Will record TSK-500 → fixed + self-validate with the re-run's

## LOG +117 (2026-06-08, autonomous tick — TSK-503 fixed: deterministic Base64 decode + host teeth)
- **TSK-503 driven reported→…→fixed** (validated pending the headless gate). `TextTools.base64Decode`
  used `Data(base64Encoded:.ignoreUnknownCharacters)`, whose all-junk handling DIVERGES by Foundation
  version AND by input length. **Reproduced on the HOST** (macOS 26 / Darwin 25.2.0), not just the VM:
  the original `testBase64Decode_invalidReturnsNil("!!!")` passed only by luck — "!!!" is length-3 (bad
  quantum → nil), but a length-4 all-junk input like `"@@@@"` strips to empty → empty `Data` → `""`
  (NOT nil) on macOS 26. So it's a real host-reproducible correctness bug, fully host-validatable.
- **Fix** (Sources/ViewerCore/TextTools.swift): strip whitespace ourselves + decode with STRICT
  `Data(base64Encoded:)` (dropped `.ignoreUnknownCharacters`); empty / whitespace-only → `""` (keeps the
  `base64Decode(base64Encode("")) == ""` round-trip). Now deterministic on every OS: any non-alphabet
  char → nil; no silent mid-string junk-strip (`"ab@cd"` → nil, not `"abcd"`). Net −1 line vs the
  original (an earlier draft added an explicit alphabet validator + helper; dropped it as redundant
  with strict decode — minimal is better).
- **Test** (Tests/ViewerCoreTests/TextToolsTests.swift): `testBase64Decode_rejectsNonAlphabetDeterministically`
  pins `"!!!"/"@@@@"/"ab@cd"/"a-_b"` → nil and `""/"   \n "` → "". Host TextToolsTests 14/14 green.
  **TEETH demonstrated on host:** reverting to the original `.ignoreUnknownCharacters` impl makes the new
  test fail 2 assertions on the host (`"@@@@"` → "" ; whitespace-only → nil); restored → green.
- This is a pure-logic ViewerCore fix → **host-self-validatable** (no VM needed). The VM lane (TSK-501)
  would also confirm cross-platform, but the host repro makes it unnecessary for validation.

- After draining the PORT `fixed` lane, picked the one cleanly-actionable NEW feature: **TSK-206**
  ([PORT][WEB] hex search) — `triaged`, front-end-only, no-dep, host-validatable. It's the web twin of
  the shipped TUI hex search (TSK-205) and completes the W1 hex-search pair. (All other actionable board
  work is owner-gated: TSK-234/235/236/243/250/255–258 await decisions/dep-approval; TSK-266/267/282 are
  VM-gated SwiftUI perf.)
- **Built (commit pending), `rust-core/crates/web/src/main.rs` only — consumes the already-tested core
  `hex::hex_search`:** new `?hexq=<query>&?hmatch=<i>` params on `/view`. In HEX mode the query is
  auto-detected as whitespace-separated hex byte pairs or, failing that, a literal ASCII string — exact
  **TUI parity** (`hex_search_parse(Hex)` non-empty ⇒ Hex, else Ascii). Each match's byte offset maps to
  its dump ROW (`offset / 16`, the new `HEX_BYTES_PER_ROW` mirroring core `view::HEX_WIDTH`) and steers
  the SAME `gutter_html` line-anchor + `.cur` machinery find / go-to-line already use — so a hex match
  scrolls natively via `#L<n>` with ZERO new JS. New `hex_find_box` (mirrors `find_box`): query input +
  `i of n` count + wrapping prev/next links bumping `?hmatch=`. HEX-mode-only (gated, so it can't collide
  with the text content-find box). Hex search takes target precedence over find / go-to-line.
- **Host teeth (5 new web tests, all green; web 61→66):** `hex_search_hex_pattern_anchors_matching_row_and_counts`
  (2 `ab cd` matches at offsets 2/34 → rows 0/2 → `1 of 2` + `id="L1"` + `hexq=abcd`/`hmatch=1` nav),
  `hex_search_hmatch_selects_the_second_match` (`2 of 2` + `id="L3"`), `hex_search_ascii_fallback_matches_text_bytes`
  (`"NEEDLE"` → ASCII fallback, offset 20 → `id="L2"`), `hex_search_no_match_reports_state` (`no matches`),
  `hex_search_box_is_hex_mode_only` (text mode must NOT surface the box). These are real teeth — without
  the `hexq` handling `hex_nav` is empty, so the `hexfind` box, counts, and anchors all vanish and every
  assert fails. **rust-core gate GREEN** (`^RCGATE_EXIT=0`): clippy no-panic + `cargo test --workspace`
  + ffi no_panic + doctests.
- Adding 2 params to `render_view_filtered`/`content_html` broke all 11 positional call sites (Rust has no
  default args) — updated each (the [[reference_swift_defaulted_param_link_break]] lesson, Rust edition).
  Net: TUI + web now at parity on hex search; the W1 hex-search pair (205 TUI + 206 web) is complete.

  line) — the EXACT trap I keep citing. Fixed to split on the LF *scalar* before commit. `swift build` clean;
  central headless gate PASSED on the committed commit.

## LOG +143 (2026-06-08, autonomous tick — TSK-502 VM pixel-lane: rebuilt + diagnosed + parked w/ precise finding)
- Owner RESOLVED the TSK-502 park (granted Screen-Recording TCC on the VM) → pursued it as the single
  highest-leverage unblock (it gates phase-2 of all 7 no-dep cores + VM bugs like TSK-452). Verified the
  VM end-to-end: re-synced; **fixed a build blocker** — a prior `sudo` build left ~1037 root-owned files
  in the VM `.build`, so `build-app.sh` failed with `ModuleCache …Operation not permitted`; fixed via
  `chown -R vm-tester .build` (keeps cache; rsync excludes .build so it's VM-local). Rebuilt
  `dist/TextView.app` fresh (Swift 6.3, ad-hoc signed). Ran the two T5 suites under the GUI session
  (`launchctl asuser 501`): **6 tests, 0 failures, but ALL 6 SKIPPED** at the `screencapture -l<id>` guard.
- ROOT CAUSE (read the SIP system TCC.db): `kTCCServiceScreenCapture` is allowed for `/bin/bash` + `Terminal`
  but NOT `xctest`. The tests spawn screencapture from inside xctest, whose TCC responsible-process is xctest
  → denied. A direct full-screen `screencapture -x` via the bash chain DOES capture (9.4MB PNG), proving the
  /bin/bash grant is real — the gap is purely xctest attribution. An agent can't add the xctest grant (SIP
  blocks sqlite/tccutil INSERT). **Parked TSK-502 (decision)** with 3 options: owner grants Screen Recording
  to the swiftpm xctest runner / I try a `/bin/bash -c "screencapture …"` wrapper workaround / LaunchAgent the
  app (un-bridge from asuser). main unaffected (tests skip, never fail; host gate green). Lessons → LESSONS.md.
- Also this tick: TSK-514 (DiffStat) driven to **validated** + logged (+142); TSK-483 verified STALE (the
  Swift `CSVSession` it cites was removed by the Rust-CSV migration — commented, recommended dismissal);
  audit #276 (IndentDetector CRLF) confirmed ALREADY-FIXED on the Swift side (LF-scalar split in place).

## LOG +139 (2026-06-10, autonomous tick — TSK-593 fixed: diff window pins top-left)
- **Root cause:** the diff tab's two-axis `ScrollView` centers content smaller than the viewport —
  nothing anchored it (the #133 side-panel fix never covered this container). **Fix (b198275):**
  GeometryReader feeds the viewport into `DiffView.scrollBody`, which expands the file-block stack to
  at least viewport size anchored `.topLeading`; large diffs scroll unchanged.
- **Oracle lesson (also in the test header):** `ScrollView` is opaque to EVERY headless oracle — a
  window-free NSHostingView frame-walk realizes zero NSViews for SwiftUI-drawn rows, and ImageRenderer
  draws nothing through ScrollView. The contract is therefore pinned one level below it: ImageRenderer
  renders the extracted `scrollBody` tree and asserts the non-transparent pixel bounding box hugs the
  top-left. ImageRenderer is legitimate HERE (pure-SwiftUI geometry, no representable, no on-screen
  visibility claim — distinct from the banned TSK-488 false-green class). Teeth demonstrated
  (alignment dropped → red). Gate green on the committed commit; bundle reinstall kicked.

## LOG +166 (2026-06-10, autonomous tick — TSK-619 fixed: launch-time grammar warm-up kills the first-open main stall)
- **Root cause:** `HTMLRenderer`'s fence path tokenizes SYNCHRONOUSLY on the main actor
  (`HTMLRenderer.swift:261` via the `renderPage` memo), so the first fence of each language
  paid the one-time `Query` compile on main — 403ms debug / ~130ms release for swift
  (measured in the TSK-592/598 captures, not guessed).
- **Fix (1466331):** `TreeSitterEngine.warm(_:)`/`isWarm(_:)` + a utility-priority
  `Task.detached` in `applicationDidFinishLaunching` precompiling all grammars. The
  engine's per-language compile locks already serialize concurrent first-touch, so the
  background warm is the designed-for path; a racing open waits only the remainder of the
  single compile it needs. `TreeSitterWarmupTests` (3, fresh-engine both-polarity) + golden
  tokenization parity; host gate green on the committed commit. Board: fixed,
  live-validation residue (the main.swift invocation itself has no headless guard — next
  `vm-profile.sh` open capture should show `ts.query-compile` gone from the open path).
- **Board hygiene note:** the owner RESOLVED the TSK-598 MountedPanesLRU park with no
  option selected (seq 3845, empty payload). Interpreted as cleared-not-approved — the
  supervised WebView-hot-zone session stays ungated work I will NOT start without an
  explicit approval (race history #213/#217).

## LOG +172 (2026-06-10, autonomous tick — TSK-617 VALIDATED: emptyFileHex was a real routing bug, not a flake)
- **TSK-617 (both halves) → validated.** The emptyFileHex UAT "timing flake" was a REAL
  user-facing bug: a 0-byte file defeats the NUL-byte binary sniff (empty input decodes as
  valid empty UTF-8), so `DocumentController.open`'s text path claimed it and the app landed
  in **Source** mode; the UAT contract is 0-byte unknown → **HEX**. The 3.0s settle bump
  (fca2114) failing identically refuted the timing hypothesis. Fix (c3e6e5b): auto-detected
  `.unknown` + size==0 routes to the binary loader before the text decode; forced "Open As…"
  categories bypass; non-empty unknowns keep text-first. 4 host behavior tests with a teeth
  demo (fix stashed → red → restored). Gate green @ c3e6e5b (first run's FoldBench 263ms was
  the known under-load bench flake; clean re-run, zero non-bench failures).
- **Two VM-lane traps burned this validation, both now codified:** (1) the post-fix VM rerun
  STILL failed because `test-in-vm.sh test` doesn't rebuild `dist/` and `dist/` is
  rsync-excluded — the T4 UAT spawned a PRE-FIX app (binary mtime predated the fix). Rebuild
  `dist` on the VM (`build-app.sh debug`) before any live-app rerun. (2) That rebuild uses the
  VM's default Swift **6.1.2** while `test-in-vm.sh` selects **6.3**; they share
  `.build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug`, so the next test compile died on "module compiled with
  Swift 6.1.2 cannot be imported by the Swift 6.3 compiler". Cure: `rm -rf
  .build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug` ONLY (never checkouts/repositories — offline mirror).
  After both: `test_VM_04var_emptyFileHex` PASSED (6.7s) against the fixed bundle.
- Owner app refreshed via `build-app.sh release --install`.

## LOG +173 (2026-06-10, autonomous tick — TSK-267 VALIDATED: 1MB HEX stall measured, fixed, regression-guarded)
- **TSK-267 → validated.** The "1MB HEX extremely slow" stall was TextKit 2 full-document
  layout of ~65k rows, measured on the VM signpost/Time-Profiler harness at every step.
  Fix chain (commits dbf155c, ab52c3e, c0e80bd, 92b5129): scoped highlight clear
  (`HexHighlightPlan`, no more O(document) removeAttribute per search edit) · ≤256KB sync
  one-shot dump build (kills the 6KB-class per-open machinery) · arithmetic grid frame
  (rows×TK2-measured lineHeight, self-sizing off) · `textContainerOrigin` override
  returning the inset (the default impl derives it from usage = full ensureLayout,
  re-triggered from layoutViewport AND renewGState). Verified-build trace: ensureLayout
  samples 1322→1, textContainerOrigin 1311→0, main-thread busy 2111→592 in the open
  window; chunkedBuild 1.82s→663ms debug / 261ms release. Guards on every host gate:
  HexFixedGridFrameTests + HexGridGeometryTK2Tests (formula == TK2 usage EXACTLY) +
  HexHighlightPlanTests, teeth demonstrated. VM ViewModesUATTests 13/13.
- **Dead end kept for the record:** bounding the text container (30fdc32) defeats TK2's
  lazy layout for in-bounds content — reverted in c0e80bd; the container must stay
  unbounded while the FRAME is pinned.
- **Measurement-integrity catch:** three "after" captures profiled STALE binaries —
  `vm-profile.sh` piped the VM build through `| tail`, masking a failure on root-owned
  `.build` debris. Fixed (b1849c4): the script now propagates the build's real exit code
  and refuses to profile. The trace that "refuted" the origin override was the stale one;
  the verified rebuild proved the override works.

  click in blank space right of a narrow grid no longer clears the click-highlight (ESC
  still does). Flagged for the owner on the ticket rather than guessed at.

## LOG +176 (2026-06-10, autonomous tick — TSK-620 half A: the ui-click real-event interaction layer lands)
- **The harness gap behind all four VM-held P1s is closed** (522576a, gate green): new
  `ui-click` / `ui-double-click` script verbs locate a view by accessibility id on the
  realized NSView tree, build the genuine AppKit event sequence (down/up pairs, clickCounts,
  cmd/shift flags, bounds-fraction positioning) and POST it to the app's event queue — the
  channel real input arrives on. `UIClickSpec` (ViewerCore) is strict: a typo'd modifier
  fails the parse instead of degrading into an unmodified click. Host tests 9/9.
- **Two constraints the tests themselves discovered, now documented in code:** (1) a
  `sendEvent` down/up pair can NEVER satisfy an NSControl tracking loop — `mouseDown` pulls
  the mouse-up from the QUEUE via `nextEvent` (first implementation went red on exactly
  this); (2) an unordered window has no window device (`windowNumber <= 0`), so queued
  events can't route to it — end-to-end delivery proof is VM-only BY CONSTRUCTION, which is
  precisely the lane those four tickets are held for.
- TSK-620 filed/triaged/in-progress on the board with the half-B plan: one VM T4 suite
  driving TSK-313 (strip double-click → ~ session), TSK-314 (+ → prefilled prompt; needs an
  NSTextField describe in DiagnosticDump first), TSK-522/523 (cmd-click log rows → selection
  bar + model), then validate all four off its evidence.

## LOG +177 (2026-06-10, autonomous tick — TSK-620 half B: in-process click delivery hits the AX wall; checkpoint + next design)
- **Verdict (decisive, from a verified-fresh binary):** in-process synthesis CANNOT reach
  SwiftUI controls by accessibility id. The versioned trace from VM run uat6 —
  `click[v4](mdv.sessionTab.new): NOT FOUND; axRootChildren=0 axIdsSample=[]` — proves the
  in-process accessibility tree is EMPTY: SwiftUI materializes AX elements only for
  external AX clients, and xctest AX TCC is owner-only (SIP blocks agent INSERT). Five
  constraints mapped en route (sendEvent vs tracking loops; unordered-window routing;
  non-key click swallowing; NSHostingView ids not on NSViews; empty in-process AX tree) —
  full entries in LESSONS.md "in-process event synthesis".
- **What landed and stays (gate PASSED on db1cec1):** the verbs + strict `UIClickSpec`
  grammar (6 tests), `UIEventSynth` with host-pinned `events()` builder (3 tests),
  activate/makeKey delivery fix (e692846), versioned self-describing NOT-FOUND trace with
  AX sample (db1cec1), `uiClickTrace` step-dump channel, `nsTextField` dump node (proven
  on the VM: real rendered field values), and `InteractionUATTests` — the ready acceptance
  harness for whichever delivery mechanism wins.
- **Checkpoint on the board (TSK-620 comment, seq 4022) with the NEXT DESIGN:** SwiftUI-side
  click-target registration — a `.uiClickTarget("mdv.x")` modifier publishing each opted-in
  control's global frame into a `ClickTargetRegistry` (onGeometryChange), consulted by
  `resolveTargetRect` BEFORE the NSView walk; coordinates feed the existing event builder
  unchanged. Fallback: the external XCUITest L4 target (testmanagerd synthesizes entitled
  events). TSK-313/314/522/523 stay correctly held at `fixed` pending that evidence.
- Process: af8bd21 briefly landed non-compiling code via a `;`-chained commit after a
  remote build — fixed in db1cec1; rule (gate commits on the build's REAL exit) added to
  LESSONS.

  constraints 6–8 landed in LESSONS: root apps are refused key status in a user session
  (cure: console-user spawn, now in AppLauncher); fork/exec'd apps can never self-activate

  word — synthesized NSEvents do not drive SwiftUI gestures even on a key+active window
  (WindowServer/CGEvent-backed input required ⇒ owner-only AX grant). Future SwiftUI
  interaction tickets go straight to exact-closure verbs + rendered-outcome assertions.
- **Kept infrastructure** (all host-tested): ClickTargetRegistry + `.uiClickTarget`
  (SwiftUI frames → ui-click, works end-to-end for resolution), ui-click/ui-double-click
  verbs (full delivery for AppKit-backed targets), console-user spawn, LS-launch mode,
  `session-new-via-goto` verb, nsTextField dump channel.

  as the TSK-621 cache lesson: a later wholesale replace can hide an intermediate
  corruption — assert at the corruption window, not after convergence.

## LOG +210 (2026-06-11 tick — TSK-624: WKWebView failure paths were UNIMPLEMENTED; fixed)

The cheap discriminator (inspect the loadToFinish end-sites) found a real defect behind the
truncated 17s interval: MarkdownRenderedView's Coordinator implemented ONLY didFinish — no
didFail, no didFailProvisionalNavigation, no webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate. Consequences:
a failed load or WebContent renderer death (jetsam is routine under memory pressure) leaked the
signpost token AND left `lastHTML` claiming the page was current, so updateNSView never re-issued
the load — blank/spinner forever with no recovery (the classic WKWebView white-screen footgun;
matches the historical "endless spinner, retry loads fast" class and is a credible mechanism for
the owner-felt "delay in opening files").

Fix `96354f3`: every navigation outcome routes through an idempotent endLoadToFinish(); the two
didFail paths drop the dedup baseline (next update re-issues the load); process-termination
additionally resets documentReady and nudges webView.reload(). RenderedLoadFailureRecoveryTests
(3) drive the exact delegate methods against a windowless WKWebView — teeth: muting the
baseline-clear → 3 red → restored green. Headless gate PASSED on the committed commit.

Board: TSK-624 → fixed (advance walk). Remaining in its scope: the 60s VM trace + paired
screencapture to discriminate real-load-slowness vs VM-software-rendering for the 17s magnitude.
Fresh bundle building + installing to /Applications.

  `testABIVersion_linkedLibraryMatchesCompiledHeader` is THE skew detector — header const vs linked

  3 asserts) → restored → 13/13 green. Both gates green on deb7c2e (rust-core: header-drift OK +

## LOG +423 (2026-06-13 — TSK-357: Format minified JS — dependency-free lexical re-indenter)

Autonomous tick. Host-actionable user-facing **feature** pick (owner redirect: bug fixes + feature
requests over the VM validation tail). Closed the named gap in TSK-357: JSON+XML pretty-print already
shipped; JS was explicitly deferred "pending a third-party parser". Added JS support to `Formatter`
WITHOUT any dependency.

**Shipped TSK-357 (commit `bbbc858`, headless gate green — 5219 tests, 0 fail, no heavy-tier leak):**
`Formatter.prettyPrintJS` — a lexical-state machine (no AST, no parser) that restores block structure
by inserting newlines + indentation around `{` `}` and statement-ending `;`, while tracking string /
template (incl. `${…}` interpolation) / line+block comment / regex context. Regex-vs-division uses the
standard preceding-token heuristic. **Safety invariant:** it only ever rewrites whitespace OUTSIDE
literals — every other byte is preserved in order — so it can never alter code meaning; Pretty-Print is
a display-only transform (`DocumentModel.displayedText`) regardless, so zero data-loss risk. Auto-wired:
`SupportedFormat.detect` gains js/mjs/cjs (jsx/ts excluded — unmodelled syntax), so the existing
Pretty-Print command (`view.prettyPrint`), menu (`main.swift:1407`), format toggle and `supportsFormatToggle`
gate light up for `.js` with no call-site changes.

**Tests (host-safe, ViewerCoreTests.FormatterTests, +13):** a differential `jsSignificantContent`
invariant — an INDEPENDENT lexer must agree byte-for-byte between input and formatted output (catches
char drop/reorder); verbatim literal-preservation (regex-with-braces, string-with-braces, block comment,
template stay intact); idempotence over an 18-case corpus; regex-after-`return`; js/mjs/cjs detection +
jsx/ts exclusion. **TEETH:** broke regex detection (treat every `/` as division) → `literalsArePreservedVerbatim`
+ `regexAfterReturn` went RED (a `{` inside `/a{2,3}/` mis-read as a block injects a newline into the
regex) → restored. NOTE: the differential invariant alone did NOT catch this (both independent lexers bail
on the newline-in-regex identically, so their stripped projections still matched) — which is exactly why
the explicit verbatim-substring tests exist as the dedicated literal-corruption guard.

Self-validated to `validated` (output-/behavior-pinned host tests with demonstrated teeth; pure-logic
engine behavior, no render path). Also recorded a precise partial-completion + deferral note on **TSK-564**
(FFI double-copy, S4): zero-copy infra exists + used on the CSV-handle paths; eliminating copy #2 on the 8
envelope methods needs a deliberate `CoreTransport` seam contract change (body `[UInt8]?` → zero-copy
`ArraySlice` view) that belongs with the remote-carrier work, not a solo S4 rush.

## LOG +419 (2026-06-13 — correction + hygiene: TSK-583 dismissed ALREADY-BUILT; 543 diagnosis corrected; safe pool drained)

No code shipped — a board-state correction tick (read-before-build caught a phantom). Went to FINALLY implement TSK-583
(the CoreRuntime/DocId registry I'd flagged for several ticks as the held high-value architectural thread)... and found it
ALREADY EXISTS. `rust-core/crates/ffi/src/handle.rs` IS the registry: an Arc-backed global `Mutex<HashMap<usize,
Arc<SessionHandle>>>` keyed by a monotonic NEVER-REUSED token (NEXT_TOKEN, 1-based), with `lookup` (Arc-clone, survives a
concurrent free), idempotent `free` (registry remove), and bogus/stale/null tokens looked-up→None→status (never a raw
deref). It was built AS the TSK-541 (validated) fix. The token is typed `*mut SessionHandle` for cbindgen ABI-stability
(byte-identical, never dereferenced) rather than a named u64 — a cosmetic delta that fulfills 583's intent.

- **TSK-583 → dismissed already-fixed** with proof: 58 mdvcore-ffi cargo tests green incl. the 3 registry tests
  (into_raw_registers_and_free_unregisters, free_invalidates_token_but_inflight_clone_survives,
  double_free_and_bogus_token_are_safe_noops).
- **TSK-543 comment CORRECTED:** my prior "543 is blocked on an unbuilt 583" was WRONG. The registry exists; cm_apply is
  STATELESS BY DESIGN, so making it stateful is a BOUNDED extension of handle.rs (register an editor doc), NOT new infra.
  543's real gates are the migration-intent DECISION (Rust-as-applier vs local-apply) + whether the cost even bites today
  (only on the Rust cmEdit path; Swift CMEditApplier applies locally with zero FFI, gated by the TSK-649 soak).

## LOG +416 (2026-06-13 — diagnosis + hygiene tick: TSK-543 architectural blocker diagnosed; TSK-672 (Git P1) dismissed already-built)

No code shipped this tick — an honest diagnosis + board-hygiene firing (the safe single-tick pool has thinned; the
high-value remaining work is architectural rust-core that needs a deliberate multi-tick effort + an owner decision, not a
blind solo change).

**TSK-543 spike (cm_apply FFI full-doc traffic) → architecturally blocked, diagnosis recorded on the ticket:**
cm_apply is STATELESS — request `{base:<whole doc>, edits}`, response `{text:<whole applied doc>}`; the full doc crosses
BOTH ways because Rust has no retained doc (needs base up) and Swift consumes the returned text as the canonical
EditorBuffer doc (needs it down). Eliminating the UP traffic requires a STATEFUL Rust doc-by-session = **TSK-583**
(CoreRuntime registry + DocId), which is unbuilt → 543 DEPENDS on 583. Also: the cost only materializes on the Rust
cmEdit path (the Swift CMEditApplier applies LOCALLY with zero FFI; governed by the TSK-649 default-ON soak), and a
"skip-FFI local apply" alternative is an owner/migration decision (Rust-as-applier vs perf). Not implemented blind.
**Sequence for a future tick: TSK-583 (stateful CoreRuntime/DocId) → then 543.**

**TSK-672 `[WISH][P1] Git stuff (diff, log, status, blame)` → dismissed already-fixed (proof attached):** all four ship
today — DiffView (per-hunk colored), GitLogTab (topological graph + message search), GitStatusTab, blame
(FileHistory + blame gutter + GitBlameParseTests), plus Stash/Remotes/Worktrees tabs. 43 git host tests pass fresh on
main. A generic wishlist item fully covered; re-file a specific gap if wanted.

**DECISION NEEDED (owner, surfaced):** the editor-perf win (TSK-543) is gated on whether to build the stateful
CoreRuntime/DocId foundation (TSK-583, the remote-core enabler) and on the Rust-cmEdit-vs-local-apply migration intent.
That's the next high-value rust-core thread when it's worth a multi-tick deliberate effort.

"kills only target pid — grandchild can leak fds/threads") — but a spike found it's ALREADY FIXED + regression-tested:
PluginSubprocessHost isolates the child in its own process group (setpgid) + killpg's the whole group on timeout, then a

dismissed `already-fixed` with the passing-checks artifact (board hygiene, like TSK-724).

## LOG +414 (2026-06-13 — TSK-361: large-file / long-line open HANG fixed (force soft-wrap); USER-FACING BUG, priority #1)

Autonomous tick. Board scan surfaced a real **user-facing bug** in the reported pool — TSK-361 "clicking large files (e.g. a
jupyter notebook) got stuck and had to kill" — which outranks the feature lane (priority #1). Took it.

**Spike (Explore agent, file:line root-cause):** a `.ipynb` is JSON text → content-sniffs as text → opens in the read-only
source `NSTextView`. NSTextView's HORIZONTAL layout is superlinear in line WIDTH, and notebooks carry base64 image blobs as
multi-MB SINGLE LINES → multi-second main-thread hang on `setAttributedString`/`glyphRange`. The existing guards
(off-main >64MiB, 512KB highlight bail, 4MB md / 50MB CM6 caps, 512MB read ceiling) ALL key on TOTAL SIZE — none on LINE
LENGTH — so a sub-64MiB long-line file loads synchronously into the hang-prone view. Gap confirmed.

**Shipped (commit `f2d19d0`, headless gate green — 5192 tests, 0 fail, no heavy-tier leak):** new pure `SourceWrapPolicy`
(ViewerCore): `hasLongLine` (early-exit scalar scan, resets at \n/\r) + `effectiveWrap(userWrap,text)` = pref OR a line
≥ 100k chars. Wired into `SourceTextController.apply` — forces soft-wrap BEFORE the text is laid out (the wrap block
precedes `applyAttributedString`), bounding NSTextView layout to the viewport width regardless of the user's wrap pref.
Same O(N)-per-apply cost class as the existing `utf8.count` (early-exits on the pathological case). Content stays visible
(wrapped) — no lockout/placeholder.

**Tests (host-safe):** ViewerCoreTests `SourceWrapPolicyTests` (8 — short-lines-safe, one-long-line-detected, threshold
inclusivity, line-break reset incl. CRLF/CR, long-line-after-short, empty/zero-threshold, effectiveWrap pref+forced).
**TEETH:** neutered the detection → 4 long-line tests RED → restored. The FIX DECISION is host-pinned; the live "no-hang
on open" confirmation is the VM/owner residual (force-kill repro can't be reproduced headlessly). → review.

**Residual (noted on ticket):** force-wrap is a strong mitigation (bounds horizontal layout); a truly extreme single line
(tens of MB) may still be slow on the linear scan/scroll paths — a follow-up could route those to a placeholder + HEX
(the markdown-placeholder pattern). The `.ipynb` categorization (currently `.unknown`→source-via-sniff) is orthogonal and
left as-is (the wrap fix is category-agnostic, covering minified JS/CSS/JSON too).

## LOG +397 (2026-06-13 — TSK-580 close-out: the thin-waist FFI envelope is now the UNIVERSAL production dispatch path)

- **TSK-580 (thin-waist FFI envelope) → validated (close-out commit `18da813`, headless gate green).** The 3 raw/aux
  production Swift wrappers — `mdvCoreHexRender`, `mdvCoreHexSearch`, `mdvCoreIndentDetect` — were the LAST direct callers
  of their dedicated per-method C symbols; they now route through the single `mdvcore_call(MDV_METHOD_*, req, aux, out)`
  envelope via a new `mdvEnvelopeCallAux` helper (CoreClient.swift). The helper carries the **aux bulk side-channel**
  zero-copy (no `[UInt8]` copy of a multi-MiB file) and returns RAW `out_buf` bytes unframed, so the caller disambiguates
  frame output (HexSearch `{offsets}`) from raw payload (HexRender/IndentDetect dumps). Each wrapper builds the small
  scalar `req` as a **named map** matching the Rust `*AuxRequest` structs (`with_struct_map`): `{width,total_byte_count,
  is_truncated}`, `{query,mode}`, `{sample_lines}`.
- **NET:** every stateless method (the 8 frame methods via the CoreTransport seam in slice 4, plus these 3 raw/aux) now
  dispatches through the ONE envelope entry — the single seam a remote `mdv-serve` carrier exposes (the transport-agnostic
  / remote-core goal). **No production Swift code calls any per-method C symbol anymore** — they're dead exports kept only
  for the coexistence soak.
- **Validation (host, teeth):** new `EnvelopeRawAuxRoutingTests` pin the migrated wrappers to the exact fixed outputs the
  Rust `envelope_routes_*` A/B tests assert (independent ground truth); the `HexRender/HexSearch/IndentDetect ABTests`
  corpora re-verify byte-for-byte parity vs the Swift engines THROUGH this path. TEETH: dropping `aux` in the helper →
  **36 failures** across all three corpora (empty dump / `[]` / `"—"` = the aux-dropped signature), mutant compiled +
  ran → restored to 0. Central headless gate green on the committed commit (5108 tests).
- **Remaining slice (b) — deleting the now-dead per-method C symbols — filed as `TSK-820`** (deferred for soak; blocked on
  re-pointing the FFI A/B oracle off the symbols first). The COLLAPSE (routing) is done; only the symbol DELETION cleanup
  remains, so the functional feature is complete.

## LOG +389 (2026-06-13 — TSK-815 markdown Dark-Mode fix landed; OWNER /Applications build → caught + fixed a TSK-813 host-build regression (TSK-816))

- **TSK-815 → fixed (commit `557ce7d`): the Dark-Mode payoff.** New `ThemeDefinition.pageCSS()` overrides
  markdown.css's `:root` vars (`--mdv-bg`←background, `--mdv-fg`←foreground, `--mdv-fg-secondary`←gutterText,
  `--mdv-code-bg`←gutterBackground, `--mdv-link`←accent) from the active theme; `themedExtraStylesheet` composes
  pageCSS + tokCSS (appended after markdown.css → wins by cascade). So a selected dark theme now darkens the
  rendered-markdown READING page, not just syntax tokens (it followed SYSTEM appearance before). nil theme →
  shim only, byte-identical (pinned). Host-tested (pageCSS var mapping, link-omitted-without-accent,
  themedExtraStylesheet present/absent; teeth drop-`--mdv-bg`→red). Render guard (VM content-region color
  assertion) is the follow-up; closing it closes TSK-641 → unblocks 642.
- **OWNER asked for an /Applications build → surfaced + fixed a regression (TSK-816 → validated, `1a47f1d`).**
  `build-app.sh debug --install` had been silently broken on the HOST since TSK-813 (573bf0f): select_toolchain's
  `newest=$(ls -d …/swift-6.*-RELEASE.xctoolchain | sort -V | tail -1)` aborts under `set -euo pipefail` when
  the glob matches nothing (the host has no such toolchain) — exiting before `swift build`. The VM never caught
  it (its glob matches). Fix: `|| true` on the substitution (build-app.sh + test-in-vm.sh's mirror). Verified
  build-app.sh debug --install now completes (swift build → assemble → install, EXIT=0); fresh bundle installed
  to /Applications/TextView.app (15:47), shipping the TSK-815 dark-mode fix for the owner.
- **Lesson (also LESSONS.md):** `var=$(<no-match-glob> | pipe)` aborts under `set -euo pipefail` (bash leaves the
  glob literal → ls fails → pipefail) — guard such substitutions with `|| true`. `main` headless-gate-green.

  emptyState ids; after `.contain` they appear). Models were already host-tested (landingRecents cap;
  newTextFileForLanding). One scene now guards three tickets.
- **Codified in LESSONS.md** (saves every future render-drain item hours): the VM AX lane surfaces only PROMOTED
  elements; `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` is the lever; `.contain` exposes CHILD ids (assert
  those, not the wrapper); modal panels (rename/code-action) self-promote via their card material.

## LOG +381 (2026-06-13 — TSK-580 slice 3-output: the thin-waist envelope now routes EVERY stateless method, incl. the raw-output ones)

    emits the `#define`s so Swift shares the ids free (header restaged). `core::MAX_HEX_WIDTH` added for the
    safety clamp (mirrors the FFI ABI constant; the over-cap A/B test pins them equal).

    symbols keep serving during the coexistence window.

## LOG +371 (2026-06-13 — TSK-812: close the WebKit DNS-prefetch reading-activity leak [VALIDATED])

- **TSK-812 (commit `fad48cb`, reported→validated — a clean close).** TSK-643's investigation had *surfaced* but
  not *closed* a residual privacy vector: WebKit auto-prefetches the DNS for link `href` HOSTS in rendered content
  **without a click**, and the CSP (`connect-src 'none'` etc.) does NOT govern DNS prefetch (it's a DNS-layer step
  before any connection). So viewing a markdown doc with external links leaked those hostnames — *what you're
  reading* — to DNS, even with TSK-635's subresource default-deny in place.
  - **Fix:** added `<meta http-equiv="x-dns-prefetch-control" content="off">` to `HTMLRenderer.renderPage`'s
    `<head>` (the documented WebKit/Safari disable). One line; the template already had charset/CSP/viewport metas.
  - **Self-validated** (not review) on the same basis as the TSK-635 CSP guard: the meta is the load-bearing
    privacy fence, its presence is host-tested + **teeth-proven** (remove → red), and WebKit honoring
    `x-dns-prefetch-control:off` is documented standard behavior (not custom render). EGRESS.md updated.
- **Pick rationale:** broke the recent review-pile streak by deliberately seeking a **fully-headless** item that
  closes clean. A security/privacy gap that a prior investigation surfaced-but-left-open fit perfectly — high
  owner value (egress was an owner concern), headless, self-validatable. The §1.5 fixed-lane drain stays
  VM/owner-gated (flagged last tick); standing blockers unchanged (Stage B 810; perf cluster supervised).

## LOG +368 (2026-06-13 — TSK-732: unify View/Edit/split font resolution)

- **TSK-732 fixed (commit `f90bef7`, triaged→review).** User-facing editor bug: the source font looked different
  between View and Edit. Root cause — View resolves `sourceFontName` via `NSFont(name:)` → a real family, but Edit
  shipped the **same raw string** into CM6 as a CSS `font-family`, and CSS matching ≠ `NSFont(name:)` matching (a
  face/PostScript name AppKit resolves doesn't match as a CSS family) → the two surfaces could land on different
  fonts. SplitPaneView passed **no** font → always SF Mono, ignoring the user's pick.
  - **Fix:** `FontPreference.cssFamily(for:)` returns the family AppKit *actually* resolves (`NSFont.familyName`),
    so CM6 names the SAME family the View renders; nil/unresolvable → nil (CM6 keeps its monospace default = the
    View's SF-Mono nil-path). ContentView feeds CM6 `cssFamily(for: sourceFontName)` instead of the raw string;
    SplitPane's `TextDisplayView` now passes `fontName: model.sourceFontName`.
  - **Teeth:** making `cssFamily` echo the raw name turned the test red (`"Menlo-Regular"` ≠ `"Menlo"` — the
    face→family normalization that prevents the divergence). 7/7 FontPreferenceTests + headless gate green.
  - **Triage corrections:** the "Shoulder" the triage flagged (`ShoulderRailView:204/263`) is **SF-Symbol icons** —
    `.font(.system)` sizes the glyph, not a code-text surface; no change needed (triage misread it). The "View as →
    lock-icon affordance" is a UX redesign, **split to TSK-811** (a feature, not the font bug).
  - Held at review: resolution logic host-guarded with teeth; on-screen View==Edit parity is a CM6-webview pixel
    check (ImageRenderer false-green) → VM/owner tail.
- **Pick rationale:** USER-FACING editor bug (owner priority #1), triaged/groomed, headless core. Picked in 1 board
  read (the triaged lane). Standing blockers unchanged (Stage B 810 owner-decision; perf cluster supervised).

## LOG +367 (2026-06-13 — TSK-806: split pane shows unsaved edits, URL-keyed)

- **TSK-806 fixed (commit `e87a20a`, reported→review).** A user-facing editor bug (sibling of the validated
  TSK-729): the split pane's text branches rendered `file.contents` (on-disk), bypassing the live dirty editor
  buffer — so the split showed stale content while you had unsaved edits.
  - **Key correctness nuance:** the ticket suggested `displayedText(for:)`, but that keys on `tabs.selected` —
    and `splitURL` is INDEPENDENT of the active tab (DocumentModel:1847-1848 swaps split↔primary), so the split
    can show a DIFFERENT file. Using the selected-tab text would render the wrong file's edits. The fix is
    **URL-keyed**: new `DocumentModel.splitPaneText(for:fallback:)` finds the tab whose `url == splitURL`, returns
    its dirty buffer text if dirty, else on-disk fallback.
  - Wired all THREE split text branches (source `TextDisplayView`, markdown/mermaid render body, CSV table) to

## LOG +365 (2026-06-13 — TSK-580 slice 3: hex_search routes through the FFI envelope; the aux bulk side-channel gets its first real consumer)

- **TSK-580 slice 3 input-half (commit `f47d782`, both gates green) — stays in `progress`.** The thin-waist
  FFI envelope (`mdvcore_call`) had its `aux` byte-slice **reserved but dead** since slice 1. This tick wired
  its first consumer:
  - `core/dispatch.rs` `Method::HexSearch = 10` (NEXT_FREE_ID→11) → new `core/hex.rs` `search_wire_aux(req, aux)`:
    the **buffer to search rides `aux`** (zero-copy borrowed, frame-cap-exempt — a multi-MiB file would overflow
    the 16 MiB `req` frame), while `req` carries only the small `{query, mode}` (public `SearchAuxRequest`). The
    `let _ = aux` stub in `dispatch::call` is gone — `aux` is now load-bearing.
  - `ffi/lib.rs` `MDV_METHOD_HEX_SEARCH = 10` — cbindgen emits the `#define`, so Swift gets the id for free
    (header restaged). `mdvcore_call` already plumbs `aux` → **no envelope-signature change** (ABI-additive).
  - Tests with **teeth**: core dispatch route + FFI envelope-vs-`mdvcore_hex_search` byte-identical parity;
    mutation (drop `aux` → search empty) turned **both** red (mutant compiled), restored green; drift-pin
    extended to id 10.
- **Why hex *search* and not hex *render*:** `mdvcore_hex_render` returns a ~18 MB **raw** dump straight to
  `MdvBuf` (bypasses `encode_frame` — frame-cap-exempt *output*), so it does NOT fit `dispatch::call`'s
  frame-returning contract; routing it needs an **out-aux** mechanism (a second out buffer or a raw-output
  method class) — an ABI-shaping decision deferred to its own slice. Hex *search* returns a small `{offsets}`
  frame, so it fits the envelope as-is once its bulk *input* rides `aux` — the clean ABI-stable first step.
- **Pick rationale:** the owner-priority user-facing perf cluster (591/592/598/266/455) is all owner-gated on the
  **supervised** `MountedPanesLRU` session (WebView race history #213/#217 — not safe to land blind; 5 measured
  captures, awaiting approval). The groomed SECURITY/PARITY/THEMING pools are nearly all already `validated`
  (635, 636, 554, 630-633, 637, 638, 639, 642, 647, 661). TSK-580 is the live P1 rust-core contract centerpiece
  (4/5 slices already landed), headless-testable, not owner-gated — the highest-value actionable item.

## LOG +360 (2026-06-13 — TSK-564 FFI copy-2 elimination: in-place frame decode for table/snapshot)

- **TSK-564 (rust-core/FFI perf) copy-2 eliminated for the payload-scaling decoders (commit 90fcc06).** The
  Swift FFI boundary double-copied each response frame: MdvBuf→[UInt8] (copy 1) then unframe's
  `Array(frame[4...])` (copy 2). Added `MsgPackReader(_:startingAt:)` (reads the whole frame from offset 4 —
  bytes stays 0-indexed, only the cursor starts past the prefix, so bounds + `finish()` hold) + a
  `frameBodyStart` validator (same length check, no body copy); `decodeTable`/`decodeSnapshot` decode in place.
  `unframe` + its tests + the body-returning free fns untouched. Host-tested (round-trip + validate/reject) +
  teeth (offset→0 → red); headless gate green. **Fresh lane** (rust-core) after the LSP/theming streak.
  - REMAINING (564 at progress): copy 1 (MdvBuf→frame) is structurally required by the buf's defer-free
    lifetime — killing it needs a decode-inside-buf-scope refactor (cost/benefit call for an S4 finding).
- **rust-core perf lane still has items:** TSK-543 (cm_apply ships full doc across FFI per edit, S3, bigger),
  TSK-575 (clippy warn-tier hygiene), TSK-583 (DocId registry, remote-core enabler). Plus the VM/UI tails
  (641 chrome T5, 640 rename-prompt VM render + code-action picker).
- **Process note (self — REPEATED, worsening):** over-deliberated HARD mid-tick again (read ~6 tickets +
  MsgPackReader internals, oscillated between candidates for ~12 calls before committing to 564). The pick
  (bounded rust-core perf) was fine; the dithering was the waste. RULE for next tick: pick the first viable
  bounded item within 2-3 board reads and START — the gate + teeth are the safety net, not pre-analysis.

## LOG +348 (2026-06-13 overnight — TSK-736 hover-lag dedupe (fix A) → review)

- **TSK-736 FIXED → review (a1da3f1).** .onContinuousHover wrote hoveredSourceLine per pointer-PIXEL, and a
  @State write always invalidates (SwiftUI doesn't dedupe equal values), so every pixel re-bodied
  SourceModeView + re-ran the 2956-match find repaint = the lag. Fix A (the dominant lever): guard the
  write `if line != hoveredSourceLine` → intra-line moves produce zero re-bodies (per-pixel →
  per-line-crossing). Test pins the dedupe premise (lineAtPointer is line-quantized). Gate green.
- **Fix B DEFERRED** (idempotent applyFindHighlights via a paint signature): the remove-all there is the
  coordination point for the SHARED backgroundColor temp-attr (find + current-line + selection) — a naive
  skip risks stale highlights, so it needs a careful complete signature; not safe to land blind. The
  per-line-crossing repaint is acceptable, so A alone is the shippable win; B is a follow-up.
- Held at review (felt latency is render-path → VM via vm-profile.sh os_signpost on .apply).
- Overnight tally (11 ticks): 739·742·744·729·737·740·735 validated · 734/728/730/738/736 review (VM) ·

## LOG +340 (2026-06-13 overnight — TSK-734 crash fixed)

  builder called `GitClient.localBranches()`/`worktreeList()` SYNCHRONOUSLY — and SwiftUI evaluates

  crash class is structurally removed. 3 model-teeth tests (empty-before-load / publishes / per-root
  replace), teeth demonstrated (drop the publish → red). Headless gate PASSED (5028).

## LOG +324 (2026-06-13 tick — TSK-577 WireError channel now EMITS (error model v2, §2.5 Phase-1))

- **TSK-577 (`[RUST-CORE]` the documented WireError {code,message,data} channel was never emitted)
  — FIXED.** Every FFI error returned a bare status enum; the host got zero context on the most
  likely real failures (large file, malformed wire), so production diagnosis was impossible
  host-side. The `WireError` type existed + was tested but nothing WROTE it.
  - **Additive + backward-compatible:** `write_wire_error(out_buf, fault)` encodes a
    `WireError{code: status, message: fault.to_string(), data:[("kind", <encode|decode|framing|too_large>)]}`
    frame into the already-freed out_buf on error, and returns the same status — a drop-in for the
    old `Err(e) => wire_status(&e)`. Wired into the `ffi_frame_body!` macro (all 8 stateless exports)
    + the 4 session/hex frame exports. Hosts that throw on the status without reading out_buf (Swift
    today) are unaffected; the rich frame is there for those that opt in.
  - **Validation:** rust-core gate green; 3 new FFI tests with **teeth** (malformed request → out_buf
    decodes to a WireError code=4 + kind=decode; bad length prefix → kind=framing; unit covers all 4
    kinds; mutating write_wire_error to not write → 2 emission tests red, recompile-confirmed,
    restored). No new FFI export → no header change. Caught + fixed an `undocumented_unsafe_blocks`
    clippy-wall trip (12 new unsafe blocks needed `// SAFETY:` comments) that plain `cargo build`
    missed but the gate caught.
  - **Consumer follow-up filed: TSK-669** — surface the emitted detail host-side (decode out_buf on
    error → log, or enrich CoreError). Noted that enriching the Equatable `.wireError` case is an
    owner-facing API change (~8 sites + equality semantics), so prefer logging unless owner wants the
    typed detail. Keeps the channel from being write-only.

  - **Additive, ZERO wire-format change** (the key low-risk choice — no MDV_WIRE_VERSION bump, no
    Swift-decode-format change, no drift-gate churn):
    - core/session.rs: `snapshot_window_frame(offset, limit)` — projects only
      `indices[offset..offset+limit]` (panic-free `.get()` for the no-panic wall), reusing the exact
      SnapshotView wire shape (`indices` carry the ABSOLUTE row ids); a bounded window never nears
      the cap. `filtered_row_count()` — the surviving count, the one datum a window omits, served as
      a cheap scalar so NO new wire field is needed.
    - ffi/lib.rs: `mdvcore_session_snapshot_window` + `mdvcore_session_filtered_count` (via the
      TSK-541 registry lookup; CSV_SESSION capability, no new bit). cbindgen header restaged.
    - Swift: `CsvSession.snapshotWindow(offset:limit:)` + `filteredCount()` bindings.
  - **Validation:** rust-core gate green on committed 8762a58; 5 new FFI tests with **teeth**
    (mutated the window to project all indices → 4 window tests red, recompile-confirmed, restored);
    Swift ABTests round-trip green vs the rebuilt .a. Caught + fixed an `indexing_slicing`
    no-panic-wall trip (`&all[start..end]` → `.get(start..end)`) that plain `cargo test` missed but
    the gate's clippy denies caught.
  - **Consumer follow-up filed: TSK-668** — wire the CSV view to page the viewport window (the

## LOG +321 (2026-06-13 tick — TSK-541 rust-core handle free-vs-call UAF closed + VALIDATED)

- **TSK-541 (`[RUST-CORE][unsafe-ffi]` Handle free-vs-call race = UB) — FIXED + VALIDATED
  (`df250db`).** The audit's "top remaining soundness hole": the inner Mutex's `try_lock`
  guarded call-vs-call (Busy), but `free` did `Box::from_raw`→drop with NO coordination
  against an in-flight `with` borrow → freeing a handle mid-snapshot was raw UAF + dropping
  a *locked* Mutex (the exact ARC/deinit-timing misuse a Swift app commits).
  - **Fix: Arc-backed global handle registry** (`Mutex<HashMap<usize, Arc<SessionHandle>>>`).
    The token Swift holds is now an opaque registry key. A call (`lookup`) clones the Arc
    out under the registry lock then operates on its clone, so a concurrent `free`
    (registry remove) DEFERS the real drop until the call returns — no UAF, the inner
    Mutex is never dropped while locked. Bonus: double-free is an idempotent no-op (was
    heap corruption); a bogus/stale token is looked up not dereferenced (None→status,
    never UB) → `lookup`/`free` shed their `unsafe`.
  - **ABI byte-identical** (opaque `*mut SessionHandle`, never dereferenced — only a struct
    doc-comment changed → header restaged via build-rust-core.sh; neither header is
    git-tracked). Contained to handle.rs + 5 FFI call sites.
  - **Validation:** rust-core gate green on committed df250db; 41 FFI tests incl. 3 new
    TSK-541 tests with **teeth** (free skips registry remove → 2 free-invalidation tests
    red, recompile-confirmed, restored); 116 Swift RustCoreTests green vs the rebuilt .a
    (end-to-end open/call/free via CoreClient). Self-validated (host-testable + teeth).
  - Picked over the queued CSV-table features because §3/§2.5 rank a rust-core memory-safety
    fix above Swift feature-wiring. (All the directive's named greenlit pools — 635/636/554/
    634/630-633 etc. — are already validated; 541 was the standout open real item.)

## LOG (2026-06-27 cont. — audit-harden: RtfTextExtractor surrogate-pair BUG found + fixed)
- Audited the hand-rolled RTF text extractor (RtfTextExtractor.plainText, untrusted .rtf input). FOUND a real bug: RTF encodes astral codepoints (>U+FFFF, e.g. emoji) as a UTF-16 surrogate PAIR of signed-16-bit \uN tokens, but the parser ran each half through Unicode.Scalar(cp) — a lone surrogate is an invalid scalar → nil → DROPPED. So emoji/astral chars in an opened .rtf silently vanished (confirmed: "{\rtf1 \u-10179?\u-8704?}" → "" instead of "😀"). FIX: hold a high surrogate (0xD800–0xDBFF), combine it with the next low surrogate (0xDC00–0xDFFF) into the astral scalar; a stray pending-high is dropped. 4 audit tests added (surrogate-pair + \uc2-multiskip / negative-\uN-BMP / malformed-unbalanced-braces — the latter 3 were already correct = teeth). 14 RtfTextExtractorTests green. Host-fixable + host-tested (pure parser).

## LOG (2026-06-27 cont. — security audit: confined() path-traversal teeth)
- Widened the audit vein to SECURITY. confined() (rust-core/crates/web — the remote server's path-confinement chokepoint: canonicalize + component-wise starts_with, closing arbitrary-read / ..-traversal / symlink-escape) is called by every route but had NO direct test (only 2 route-integration tests referenced it). Added 5 security teeth (web/main.rs tests): root + a real under-root path allowed; ../ + nested ../.., a string-prefix sibling (component-wise containment, not string-prefix), a symlink resolving outside root, and a non-existent path (canonicalize fail-closed) all rejected. All pass — guard correct; a regression now fails the rust-core gate instead of silently opening a path-traversal vuln. Test-only; no source change.
